Title: GravaStar Mercury M2 Wireless Gaming Mouse, 5 Dynamic Lightsync RGB (White)
Description: Precision in Play: 1K Hz Polling Rate for Sharp Accuracy -Equipped with a 1K Hz polling rate and 26,000 DPI, the M2 captures every nuance of your movement, translating it into precise, in-game actions. Perfect for both competitive and casual gaming, it ensures your responses are always on point, thanks to the PAW3395.
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "De De", "review_title": "Mercury m2 mouse", "review_text": "Absolutely amazing. Upgrade from razer deathadder v3. Sounds amazing, looks amazing, feels amazing. Best value mouse for its price. Also comes with cable and stickers which is a nice touch. The mouse connects instantly with no setup required, had amazing response, and is build great. 10/10 mouse", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "ana sophia", "review_title": "Yes, it IS worth your money!", "review_text": "Fantastic mouse for gaming and work! Comfortable for smaller hands, and is really beautiful alongside the Mercury K1 keyboard in white. Worth the wait to have a matching set. I notice a huge difference between my ergonomic mouse and this one for responsiveness and DPI settings. As someone who has to use the scroll wheel a lot I find it really satisfying with good haptic feedback. Fully customizable button mapping and rgb settings puts the cherry on top. If you’ve been wondering whether it’s worth splashing out on along with the keyboard, DO IT! They make for such a clean setup, I’ve loved every bit of my Gravastar kit.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "William", "review_title": "Buy under $80 and you get an absolute GEM", "review_text": "Beautiful mouse.
The webby design is beautiful but on the right side for Claw and Fingertip Grips makes for a very awkward seat for the fingers, palm grip is not an issue because there are grated flat surfaces toward the front of each side that is very accommodating for the thumb and fingers but I personally like to grip with my fingertips curled around the side, fingertips sitting vertically in the middle rather than fully straight and riding horizontally along the side. This completely avoids that surface meant for fingers and relies on the webbed design for support which is a little off feeling. By no means does this make it unusable, you just have to get used to it. My ring fingertip generally makes contact with that grated support surface but my pinky sits further back and I have to set it on the skinny web part.
This does not make the mouse unusable I just believe it justifies $60 over $80, this oddity in the design applies to all of GravaStar's mice.
Overall the PAW3395 is the best widespread sensor to date, yes there are better sensors but they are not generational leaps, they're just small improvements and support gimmicks like 4k and 8k polling when there is no proven practical increase over 2K, the specs of this mouse and the quality of the wireless (and bluetooth)- are pretty unbeatable at $60, $80 I'd say if you really want the design of this mouse, go for it, but this thing is always on sale.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Silas Growden", "review_title": "Fantastic Design and Quality, but Too Small", "review_text": "I’m going to give this mouse 5 stars, even though I won’t be using it.
It is exactly what is pictured. The internal LED is very well-diffused and easy to customize with Gravastar’s software. The sensor is extremely accurate. The mouse has negligible latency in both configurations, and is very smooth across my mousepad. The buttons feel excellent, and the ergonomics are pretty good: buttons are where you need them to be without being in the way.
Why won’t I be using it then? The size. It’s too small for me. I was very sad when I gave it a try, and it just didn’t fill my hand as well as my other mouse (Razer DeathAdder V2 X).
Gravastar is a fantastic company that makes quality products with a distinct style. I love their keyboard, their chargers, and their speakers. My wife has the Sakura pink version of this mouse that matches her keyboard, and she LOVES it. So I would recommend this mouse on the basis of its quality and its style to anyone, with the caveat that it’s just not the best fit for larger hands. If you’re used to a smaller mouse like a Logitech, then maybe this would be close to what you’re used to anyway, but for me, I’m more comfortable on my DeathAdder.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Zarina", "review_title": "Great mouse!", "review_text": "I got it as a gift for my sister! She LOVED it! It works great and looks really good.
She wanted a transparent one and it is lightweight, smooth and easy to connect to the laptop.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "casey S", "review_title": "Super beautiful. Low latency. Wish it was Bigger", "review_text": "Ive been using this mouse for about a month now, so far its golding up well! The mouse is beautiful. What I love about Gravastar is their unapologetically futuristic cyberpunk designs. The look of the mouse is beautiful and is exactly what I was looking for when I searched "futuristic mouse".
As far as performance, I've had no issue with it at all. The latency is extremely low (practically non existent in my experience). Both wireless and wired feel very responsive. It's very lightweight also. I haven't used the windows app yet, but from what I've seen. You can customize the rgb a bit and program the 2 side buttons and the top one near the scroll wheel.
2 gripes:
1. The design of the mouse can make it difficult to wipe the inner part of the mouse. If it gets dusty. But I guess that's the trade off for a beautiful design. Not a deal breaker.
2. It's relatively small, I have fairly large hands. So it's easy for it to slip out of my hands when it gets sweaty. They're not abnormally large, but big enough to make my hand cramp up after an hour or 2 of playing.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Kenny", "review_title": "Ok... I like it!", "review_text": "You'll either love or hate the look of this mouse. Definitely a love for me! Glides effortlessly, ergonomics are perfect for me. Haven't tested the battery life yet, but it comes about 50% charged. This is my 1st product from this company so if it holds up, it'll be good vaule for money compared to bigger brands. You can choose to download the software or use their web app. You can changed RGB colors, adjust DPI, etc. Zero issues with tracking so far. Would recommend.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "with_teeth100", "review_title": "I will never use any other from now on", "review_text": "🔥 Review: Mercury M2 Wireless Gaming Mouse 🔥
The Mercury M2 Wireless Gaming Mouse is an absolute weapon in the hands of any serious gamer. From the moment I unboxed it, I could tell this wasn’t just another “me too” peripheral—it’s a precision tool built for dominance.
The wireless response time feels indistinguishable from wired, which is insane considering how most wireless mice still struggle to match that level of speed and accuracy. Every click lands instantly, every flick registers without delay. It’s as if the M2 is reading my mind before my fingers move.
The ergonomic design deserves a standing ovation. It fits the hand like it was carved for it—no awkward angles, no fatigue after hours of gaming. The textured side grips are a small detail, but they make a massive difference during sweaty high-pressure matches.
And the sensor performance? Ruthless. Tracking is flawless, even at absurd DPI ranges. Whether I’m micro-adjusting for a pixel-perfect headshot or whipping across a 4K screen in a split-second, the Mercury M2 never loses its nerve. It’s a beast that adapts to every playstyle.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Reaverz0r", "review_title": "Great mouse!", "review_text": "AMAZING mouse!
Only complaint is that the manual came in all chinese, but easy enough to work out! looks great, feels great, i am pleasantly surprised and highly reccomend!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "mouse buono se usato con il cavo", "review_title": "nice", "review_text": "ottimo, funziona benissimo!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Sergio", "review_title": "Jest super", "review_text": "Pasuje do mojej małej dłoni. Ładnie wygląda.
Jestem zadowolony z zakupu", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Logan", "review_title": "Gravastar is amazing", "review_text": "Really nice mouse, never had any issues, holds a charge for up to 2 and a halfish days, looks really nice, has a pretty good software from what I have seen, and gravastar is amazing", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Huseyin", "review_title": "Good", "review_text": "Good", "review_rating": ""}]

Title: GravaStar Mercury M1 Pro Wireless Gaming Mouse, Lightweight Magnesium Alloy, 26,000 DPI, PAW3395DM Sensor, 5 Programmable Buttons, Support Wired/2.4GHz/BT, Up to 200 Hours Battery Life (Gradient Pink)
Description: Ergonomic Precision – Play Longer, Aim Better -- Sculpted to fit your hand naturally, the M1 Pro reduces fatigue during marathon gaming sessions. Enhanced tactile buttons deliver crisp, accurate clicks—turning every move into precise, effortless action.
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Diolys F.", "review_title": "One of the Best Mice I’ve Owned", "review_text": "I bought this for both work and casual gaming, and it’s been one of my favorite desk upgrades. The sensor is responsive, the clicks are crisp, and switching between Bluetooth, 2.4 GHz, and wired mode has been seamless. Battery life has also been much better than I expected.
I was hesitant about the skeleton design before buying it, but in person it looks even better. I’ve had several people ask me what mouse it is because it’s so unique. It’s definitely not just for looks—it performs just as well as it looks.
If you’re on the fence, I’d absolutely recommend it. Great build quality, excellent performance, and a design that really stands out from every other mouse on the market. BUY IT!!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Shorty_Keeper", "review_title": "More comfortable than I thought it would be", "review_text": "I was going back and forth on getting this mouse. Gave it a go and am very pleased with it. Not exactly what I would call light weight as I have sub40g mice, but the weight is not an issue. Very nice fit and feel in my hand. Smooth, responsive and great looking design. Battery life is great too. Only thing I can say that threw me a curve was the back button is a bit proud ( protrusion) and I would accidentally hit back by mistake. Once I acclimated to the button design zero negative feedback. And that had nothing to do with the build and quality but was a me thing and not something I would justify a reduced rating. Actually like it enough I got a Gravastar Mercury X Pro and love it out of the box. The Webhub driver is nice too. 10 of 10, would buy again and recommend to a friend", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "SM", "review_title": "Great quality and unique look", "review_text": "Very impressed by the overall aesthetic and functionality of this mouse. I play a lot of games involving precise aim, and this was perfect for me. I was searching for a mouse that didn't look or feel clunky, and this design is unique and really makes a difference for me. I haven't had any issues with the DPI or lighting customization, and it feels very smooth. The lighting has different modes that you can change using the software. I use it on bluetooth alone and it always connects instantly when I turn my pc on. The charge lasts almost a week of heavy use. The quality reflects a higher-end mouse for sure.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "ina", "review_title": "decent for gaming, aesthetics, and wrist health.", "review_text": "this mouse is actually so pretty and actually decent for gaming! its lightweight which is good for ergonomics and gaming. its also a surprisingly comfortable mouse (the organic design kinda made me debate it haha but its comfy). the rgb is customizable which is awesome, and it goes well with my setup 👍 with this rgb though, it doesn’t heat up much which is ideal especially for a mouse with rgb.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Melissa", "review_title": "New favorite mouse, easy to set up and use.", "review_text": "Bought this as a gift/replacement for someone whos mouse was going out.
They absolutely loves this mouse. As in it is currently his favorite mouse (this person is tech savvy and in web dev/technology so they own quite a few mice (everything from ergonomic, 3d and trackballs)
They said this about the mouse "its lightweight and responsive and it just looks so cool" their only complaint (its minor) is that sometimes after cleaning they put the mouse back wrong and try to use it upside down. (See told ya it is minor.
The colors are vibrant enough, the design suits a cyberpunk esthetic. Mouse clicks are responsive with decent feedback (clicky)
Battery life is really good. Ive seen it get charged twice since I bought it for them. It never looses its connection to the laptop.
Another complaint (again minor) they wish is was slightly (just slightly) bigger but overall it fits comfortably in their hand (male sized hand)", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Sharlie", "review_title": "Love this Mouse", "review_text": "Teenage son is loving this mouse. I have to say we have gone thru maybe 20 for gaming. Fast response time and easy gliding on surface. Solid built mouse. Comfortable. Looks like a piece of art on your desk too", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Ajay", "review_title": "Pretty sweet mouse", "review_text": "I really like this mouse—the build quality feels great, and it offers plenty of customizable features through GravaStar’s software. I use it for everything from gaming to everyday tasks, and it performs well across the board.
It’s lightweight, and the battery life is impressive—I rarely find myself needing to recharge it. The dual connectivity options are a big plus for me. I use the USB dongle with my Windows desktop or laptop, and Bluetooth with my MacBook Air since it only has USB-C.
While there isn’t a dedicated macOS app, it hasn’t been an issue. I can adjust all my settings on my Windows machine, and since they’re saved to the mouse’s onboard memory, they carry over seamlessly when I switch to my Mac.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Kaykay", "review_title": "Its a premium mouse but not the best for gaming.", "review_text": "The quality of the product is very nice, although it's heavier then what I am use to it feels premium. Not the best gaming mouse but a very pretty one.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Michele Rubertelli", "review_title": "Il Massimo!", "review_text": "La qualità dell' M1Pro è estrema ... sia come materiali che come estetica che come funzionalità .... semplicemente il meglio sul mercato!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Jerome", "review_title": "!!!!!Ungewöhnlich gut !!!!!! Ein Meisterwerk der Kunst", "review_text": "Ich habe mir die Gravastar Mercury M1 Pro Gaming Maus vor kurzem zugelegt und bin absolut begeistert von diesem Produkt. Als leidenschaftlicher Gamer bin ich immer auf der Suche nach hochwertigem Equipment, das meine Performance verbessert, und diese Maus hat meine Erwartungen in jeder Hinsicht übertroffen.
Design und Ergonomie:
Das futuristische Design der Gravastar Mercury M1 Pro ist ein echter Hingucker. Mit ihren scharfen Linien und dem robusten, industriellen Look hebt sie sich deutlich von anderen Mäusen auf dem Markt ab. Die Ergonomie ist hervorragend; die Maus liegt perfekt in der Hand und ist auch bei langen Gaming-Sessions unglaublich komfortabel. Die Daumenauflage und die gummierten Seiten bieten zusätzlichen Halt und Kontrolle. Diese kann man zusätzlich anbringen.
Performance und Präzision:
Die Mercury M1 Pro ist mit einem hochpräzisen Sensor ausgestattet, der eine beeindruckende DPI-Range von bis zu 26.000 bietet. Diese Anpassungsmöglichkeiten sind ideal für verschiedene Spielgenres und Spielstile. Die Reaktionszeit ist unglaublich schnell, und ich habe keinerlei Verzögerung bemerkt, was besonders bei kompetitiven Spielen von entscheidendem Vorteil ist. Der 4K-Empfänger sorgt für eine blitzschnelle und zuverlässige Verbindung, was die Gesamtperformance weiter verbessert. Die Tastenanschläge sind knackig und präzise, was das Spielerlebnis noch intensiver macht.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Nina Corbet", "review_title": "Parfait", "review_text": "Parfait ! Title: Razer Basilisk V3 Customizable RGB Wired Ergonomic Gaming Mouse, Black
Description: ICONIC ERGONOMIC DESIGN WITH THUMB REST — PC gaming mouse favored by millions worldwide with a form factor that perfectly supports the hand while its buttons are optimally positioned for quick and easy access
Category: Electronics,Computers & Accessories,Computer Accessories & Peripherals,Keyboards, Mice & Accessories,Mice
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Yahia B.", "review_title": "Love the switch", "review_text": "I used the Razer Mamba Elite for many years and absolutely loved it, so I was hesitant to switch. This mouse was recommended to me as a replacement, and I have been pleasantly surprised. It feels comfortable in the hand, responds quickly, and the customizable buttons and RGB lighting are excellent. The scroll wheel is especially smooth and versatile. Overall, it has been a great change and I am very happy with it.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Amazon Customer", "review_title": "Yes! Beats the G502 Hero (which I liked) and the G502 X (by a lot)", "review_text": "Good god, what a mouse. I mean, it's not perfect; nothing is. But it's so good.
I came from years of the G502 Hero; the grips on it were wearing out. I first decided to try a G502 X, as it was supposed to be an improved version of the Hero, essentially. For $25 more than the Basilisk, it pretty much sucked in my opinion. The only thing I could imagine picking it over the Basilisk for is weight. But if you care that much about weight, there are much lighter mice on the market.
---
I'll review it as compared to the Hero (and a bit to the X), as that's what I know. They're pretty common, so maybe this will help people out if they're thinking about converting:
Initially I wasn't so sure about the grip and the main mouse buttons. The mouse buttons have a rough texture, and I found with my Hero that when my fingers were slightly tacky/damp, they would stick slightly to the surface of the buttons in the same way a clean basketball shoe does to a court (i.e., not "sticky", but grippy). I liked that. But after using it for a while, I think it's totally fine and maybe even better.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Dallas Barnes", "review_title": "One of my favorite mice and you will love it too", "review_text": "This mouse is just incredibly smooth. Even with its high weight the skates make it super easy to move around and the weight gives it control, resulting in superb aim. The material can make your hands a bit sweaty when death gripping it, but it’s very solid matte surface. You can grip test and throw this mouse across a room without it breaking. The shape this mouse has just fits right in your hand, and the rubber side grips make it super comfortable and easy to use, it’s basically great with any grip type. The skates are super glidey and quiet even when under the weight of this chunker of a mouse. It’s better for bigger hands of course, it’s harder to use with smaller hands but it’s doable. The scroll wheel is the best of any mouse, even the Logitech g502. It has a setting in the software where it can be a tactile scroll wheel when scrolling slowly, but becomes a freely spinning wheel when flicked fast. You can even switch between spinny wheel mode and tactile mode with the click of a button. I loved this mouse so much I upgraded to the wireless version, and I wasn’t sacrificing much leaving wired because the battery life was great on that one. 10/10 mouse.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Louis Barber", "review_title": "Great for the price.", "review_text": "The Razer Basilisk V3 is hands down one of the best gaming mice I've ever used. It's super comfy even during long gaming sessions thanks to its ergonomic design, and the customizable buttons are perfect for both gaming and getting stuff done. The RGB lighting looks awesome, and the HyperScroll wheel is surprisingly handy for switching between precise and fast scrolling.
The sensor is super accurate and responsive, and the mouse just glides across my mousepad. I also love how easy it is to customize everything through Razer Synapse. Whether I'm playing FPS games, MMOs, or just browsing, this mouse works perfectly.
If you want a top-notch gaming mouse with tons of customization and excellent comfort, the Basilisk V3 is totally worth it. Highly recommended!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Noah Schreiber", "review_title": "Good gaming mouse and does what it needs. Just wish it would last longer.", "review_text": "To be honest they don't make mice like they used to. I remember a time where you would buy gaming mice and they would last 5 years minimum. Now a days they last a year if you are lucky. So far this mouse has worked pretty good and seems like it is holding up quite fine. I also want to point out I haven't had this for a very long time and I suspect the build quality of the mouse should last a year if this was anything like my old razor mouse.
The scroll wheel is pretty solid. I like how responsive it is. I have never seen a mouse scroll wheel quite like this. Scrolling speed is pretty good. Was able to do a lot of jagged movements and noticed the mouse handled it very well in minecraft.
Ergonomic of the mouse are probably the best part. I haven't used a non trackball mouse that felt this great in maybe ever. The programmable buttons I haven't used for anything since I literally have nothing to remotely use them for whatsoever.
RGB is decent. Not a selling point for me that is a selling point for some people I guess.
With that said I am not sure if I can recommend this just because it seems pretty good but the way gaming mice have been going I don't see this lasting more than a year. I remember a time where mice would last like a decade now they break if you look at them the wrong way. I will say the big pro to a gaming mouse is the fact it is meant for gaming. Yes you are paying a lot of money for something that will break within a year but you pretty much have no choice just because these mice have a sensor in them that is significantly way better than most mice.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "BearFire", "review_title": "This Mouse Ruined Cheap Mice for Me", "review_text": "I’ve genuinely liked using the Razer Basilisk V3. The first thing I noticed was how comfortable it felt. Some mice are fine for about 20 minutes and then they start feeling like a weirdly shaped brick. This mouse has been much better for longer use, whether I’m gaming or just clicking around online doing whatever nonsense I got distracted by.
What I like most is that it feels like someone actually thought about how a hand works. The buttons are responsive, the movement is smooth, and the scroll wheel feels so nice that it almost made reading comment sections worth it. Almost. While this mouse has not been life changing in a dramatic movie soundtrack kind of way, it has changed my expectations enough that going back to a cheaper mouse would feel like using a shopping cart with one bad wheel.
Oh, and the customization. I am not out here trying to launch a space mission from my desk, but it is nice being able to set things up in a way that actually fits how I use it. Once everything is dialed in, it just feels easy.
Overall, it has been a genuinely solid mouse and one of those upgrades you stop thinking about because it just quietly does its job well. Which, for a mouse, is honestly the dream. It just sits there, minds its business, and makes me slightly more powerful than I probably deserve.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Troy", "review_title": "Excellent & totally worth it.", "review_text": "Best mouse I've ever used. Every surface is comfortable to touch & adds to its controllability. The RMB & LMB are soft & responsive, and have a quick reset. Easy to hold & thumb rest allows for greater control during long use.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Michael", "review_title": "Peak Gaming Mouse Energy", "review_text": "This mouse is basically the “I’m him” of gaming mice. It’s super comfortable, the buttons feel crisp, and the 26K DPI sensor tracks like it’s reading your mind. The RGB lighting goes full rave mode (in a good way), and the HyperScroll wheel is clutch whether you’re swapping weapons or doom‑scrolling.
The 11 programmable buttons give you all the customization you could want, and the whole thing just feels premium. It’s fast, smooth, and honestly makes every other mouse feel a little mid.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "KARIM FAHMY", "review_title": "Excellent", "review_text": "Very good quality", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Michael T Brown", "review_title": "Fantastic mouse for those who like it heavy.", "review_text": "I'm an avid PC user and rarely replace my accessories. My mouse especially was hard to replace, as every top end mouse seems to get lighter and lighter. However, after using the Basilisk V3, I can safely say this mouse has been a perfect upgrade from my 2013 Deathadder. It weighs roughly the same, being on the heavier side for a mouse, and that's perfect for me. It's built great, has a fantastic braided cable which is smooth to the touch, it doesn't catch on corners like the older Razer cables, and the RGB is stellar. I really like the ring of RGB that goes around the base, and it's incredibly easy to edit in Razer Synapse.
The mouse is also extremely comfortable. I didn't expect a thumb rest to do much, but I'll honestly miss it if I ever have to upgrade.
For the price, you really can't go wrong. This mouse is incredible for its price point and well worth investing in if you like to 'feel' your mouse movements.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "uae", "review_title": "perfect", "review_text": "real razer mouse not a scam works perfectly fine and great quality.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Andrew", "review_title": "The greatest strength is it's smoothness of operation.", "review_text": "I've been using this mouse for about a month now.
It's my first gaming mouse.
It's lighter than I expected but that does not impair the use at all.
The greatest strength is it's smoothness of operation. The cursor glides smoothly with small and large gestures.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Raphael Oliveira", "review_title": "ótimo mouse", "review_text": "Mouse ergonômico com encaixe para dedão, tem textura no dedão e nas laterais para um grip melhor, é grande então dá para usar se você tem pegada "garra" ou se pega com a mão inteira, funciona em ambos.
É mais pesado que os outros mouses como li descrito em reviews de sites mas é um peso ideal, mouse leve é meio estranho, na minha opinião.
Vêm com botões de várias funcionalidades, como os 2 botões acima do dedão, assim como o a frente do dedão que serve para diminuir o dpi para jogos tipo FPS, por ex, usar com sniperscope onde você precisa fazer movimentos menores. Para MOBA não serve para nada, mas todos os botões são customizáveis com o app da razer, então dá para configurar para usar algum slot de item, ou skill, etc. O app também tem como fazer macros, e configurar o padrão das cores dos leds.
O cabo tem uma qualidade boa e longo. O scroll é bem macio, e tem um botão para trocar entre modo corrido (rola sem parar) e o scroll normal (com pulos/ticks). E o próprio scroll também serve como 2 botões extras quando vc empurra ele para os lados.
De forma geral, satisfeito, principalmente com a ergonomia.", "review_rating": ""}]

Title: Logitech G PRO X2 SUPERSTRIKE Wireless Gaming Mouse - Black/White
Description: Designed With Pros, Engineered to Win: Designed alongside the world’s best esports athletes, the Logitech G PRO X2 SUPERSTRIKE wireless gaming mouse delivers the fastest, fully customizable click
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Sol", "review_title": "huge difference during long gaming sessions", "review_text": "The Logitech PRO X2 SUPERSTRIKE is easily one of the best gaming mice I’ve used. The first thing you notice is how incredibly lightweight it is—it glides effortlessly, which makes a huge difference during long gaming sessions. The responsiveness is top-tier, and the Lightspeed wireless connection feels just as fast and reliable as a wired mouse.
The build quality is excellent, with a clean, minimalist design that looks great on any setup. The clicks feel crisp and precise, and the customizable haptics add a nice touch for those who want to fine-tune their experience. Battery life is also impressive, and the USB-C charging is a welcome upgrade.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Joseanup", "review_title": "The best gaming mouse I’ve ever used", "review_text": "I’ve owned and tested many gaming mice over the years, and the Logitech G Superstrike X2 is, without question, the best one I’ve ever used. I don’t play competitively—I mostly enjoy adventure games, action titles, and other immersive experiences—but this mouse has made every gaming session more enjoyable. It combines incredible comfort, premium build quality, and features that genuinely stand out.
The biggest highlight for me is the haptic switches. They feel amazing, providing a tactile, satisfying click that makes every input feel deliberate and precise. The feedback is unlike anything I’ve experienced on another mouse, adding a level of immersion that you don’t realize you’re missing until you try it. Combined with the outstanding responsiveness, every click feels fast, consistent, and incredibly satisfying.
Another thing I absolutely love is how lightweight it is. It glides effortlessly across the mousepad and never feels fatiguing, even after hours of gaming. The shape is comfortable, the weight is perfectly balanced, and it almost feels like an extension of your hand.
The wireless connectivity has also been flawless. It’s fast, stable, and completely reliable, with no noticeable latency or dropouts. It truly delivers the freedom of wireless without any of the compromises that used to come with it.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Adnan Zilic", "review_title": "Haptic is the future for mice.", "review_text": "I gave this mouse 5 stars simply because of the haptic triggers. The mouse comes with several small 2.4 gram weights in a simple and sleek container, and I found my comfortable weight. They are easy to install with a simple twist open/lock opening on the bottom of the mouse.

I like this kind of mouse wheel action, I find the heavy bump/clicks of other mouse wheels distracting at quick scroll movements.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Rush", "review_title": "BLOWN AWAY", "review_text": "I just want to start this review by saying I don't play MMO's at all but play ARPGs, FPS, Strategy, and Roguelikes. The Venus Pro wireless is perfect as it gives you the mobility of a mobile mouse and the features of a MMO Mouse. I got this early December and I'm still getting used to it. I can say that the mouse is really comfortable even though I have slightly smaller than medium hands (Medium nitrite gloves fit me with looseness). The texture of the mouse feels really nice too and helps you know exactly what you're touching on the mouse. The side buttons do this in a different way by tilting the depth of each row so you know which row your thumb is on which is just genius design. The RGB is nice and not over the top.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Maylon", "review_title": "Amazing Mouse", "review_text": "I received this mouse about a week ago and have been using it every day since then. Honestly, I see people making up excuses that this mouse is good "for the price." Even if this mouse was worth 50 dollars, it'd still be a fair price.
-Packaging:
The mouse came in simple, straight-forward packaging. A picture of the product on the front, accompanied by flames surrounding the mouse. Nothing wrong about saving money, and it was a little funny tbh.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "IvyX", "review_title": "Updated review for Wireless Version", "review_text": "Wireless Version Review:

I decided to go back to my old (although dysfunctional) one and this year decided to try the wireless version.
Set up was surprisingly easy given how much trouble I had last time, I really like how the software and drivers come on a usb flashdrive now instead of on the website or a mini disc. This ensures you have some drivers that should make the mouse work in it's most basic iteration. It worked as soon as I plugged it in, and the flash drive as well. You can only have two profiles with the wireless version (and switch between then using the button on the bottom of the mouse), but all the buttons are still programmable and you can the light settings on the mouse or turn them off entirely if you don't like the feature or want to save battery, and you can do this on both the app or the mouse itself. [{"reviewer_name": "N.", "review_title": "Overall, a great mouse. Has become my go to.", "review_text": "I got my first basilisk mouse on a Black Friday sale, and I got hooked. I love it.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Saleem", "review_title": "Great mid range mouse option", "review_text": "My previous mice include the Razer Deathadder V2, Razer Basilisk V2 X Hyperspeed, and the Logitech Pro X Superlight.
This is easily the most comfortable mouse I've used, the contours feel perfect and the extra button the side is well placed and feels like a natural addition. Title: Logitech G502 X Plus Wireless RGB Gaming Mouse - Black
Description: Icon reinvented: From the legacy of Logitech’s most popular G502 design, G502 X PLUS is reimagined and redesigned with the latest innovations in gaming technology; available in black and white
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "J.S.", "review_title": "G502 X Plus -- A Worthy successor to earlier G502's for FPS games", "review_text": "The 2022 Logitech G502 X Plus was a very pleasant surprise. It is replacing a Logitech G-Pro that is roughly 80 grams weight on a Logitech Powerplay mouse pad (expanded cover for extra space and non-stop charging), primarily used for Overwatch2. Other gaming mice in my collection include earlier G502's, G903, Razer Death Adder + Copperhead, Steelseries Rival3 and Rival600, etc. Generally the best performers in FPS games are the lightest units with the best optical sensors, and the G502 X Plus definitely fits that criteria.
Pros:
-Comfortable ergonomic shape for marathon gaming sessions
-PTFE mouse feet for super-smooth glide across mouse pads
-The new optical hybrid switches are incredibly fast compared to the G-Pro's older Omron switches, with a nice crisp click and improved actuation. They will last much longer than conventional mechanical switches and correct double-clicking issues. My last G-Pro's right rear thumb switch suffered from double-clicking issues since they were the old Omron mechanicals that wore out from constant use.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Garrett", "review_title": "Exactly what you would expect from a direct upgrade.", "review_text": "TBH if your looking for a G502/HERO/Lightspeed replacement there is no complaints in my opinion.
Its just a hair bit wider then the previous 502s almost unnoticeable but if you hold them together there is a slight difference.
The battery life for it so far has been good for me only been having to charge it like once a week it feels like.
It feels like a upgraded 502 lightspeed which is what is.
I like that they gave us a option to replace the thumb button with a flat cover that matches the mouse curve so you dont have to have the thumb button for those of us like myself who accidentally press it and never actually use it.
Compared to what we paid at launch for the g502 it feels comparable for value and performance.
The scroll wheel feels like a nice upgrade from the deep groves to more of a slightly grooved surface thats easy to catch with your finger without issues.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Chaz A", "review_title": "Great gaming mouse", "review_text": "I've been using the Logitech G502 X Plus for about a week now, and it's been excellent so far. Title: Razer Naga V3 Pro Wireless MMO Gaming Mouse with Swappable Side Plates
Description: ADAPT TO ANY GAME GENRE – Customize your setup with 3 swappable magnetic side plates featuring 12, 6, or 2-button layouts, plus 2 quick-access edge buttons and a lockable ring finger button for MMO, MOBA, FPS, and battle royale gaming
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Albert", "review_title": "I don't like Razer, but this mouse slaps", "review_text": "I was really, really contemplating rating this less because of Razer Synapse 4. I couldn't get button remapping to work in any game at the start, it would only work after I closed Synapse entirely. Profile switching also didn't work. The software took so much finagling and trial and error manually deleting Synapse and re-installing more than once--I even tried deleting Synapse data online from my account via the Privacy Center to no avail. Midway through, I almost just resorted to keeping things on onboard memory and manually switching between games. It was brutal.
Thankfully profile switching started working and button remaps followed suit. I don't know how I got it to work, but it works! It handles so well that the pain setting up the software can be forgiven. This is everything I wanted out of my old Logitech G600s, of which I've had several and daily drove for the better part of a decade. I'd always try but ultimately return other MMO mice because I'd always miss ring-finger button. I know I'm not the only one that felt this!
It seems like Razer heard our cries and implemented it on this new Naga V3 Pro, even adding the two additional buttons by the left-click button like on the V2 Hyperspeed. My only gripes are that the side buttons aren't as pronounced and contoured as the G600, and the left- and right-mouse clicks are just obnoxiously loud. Travel distance and weight per click as well I'd say aren't great either--maybe better for older MMOs where each click needed to be more deliberate, but a lighter switch would be better for modern MMOs. I guess I'll get used to them.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "REM", "review_title": "I loved my Logitech. This is a viable replacement!", "review_text": "I am a user, and fond lover, of the G502 and G600. When I saw V3 Pro and the feature set, I really wanted to take a dive into the Razer ecosystem and give it a whirl. This one mouse had the features and potential to replace both the G600 and G502 on my desk.
While using and trying the mouse, I can say that it does replace both and works as expected. The form may cause other pause, but it comes down to preference and usability. The G502 is a great mouse but was causing wrist issues despite the perfect for. The Naga V3 Pro is slightly smaller than the V2, but it has given me the form of the G600 which tends to be usable longer for me, with the features of the G600 and G502.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Randy", "review_title": "Good MMO Mouse", "review_text": "Been using an MMO mouse for over 10 years now and this is an upgrade from my very used Trinity. Feels great in the hand but only negative is the high-pitched "ting" sound coming from Gen-4 optical switches left click.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Charlie Gerkin", "review_title": "Excellent Multi-mode mouse", "review_text": "Works great with 2, 6, or 12 side buttons. Razer Synapse customizes it with up to twice as many functions. Button on ring finger rest acts as trigger for second set on all Razer devices. Replaced my V2 with it.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Rafael Ospino", "review_title": "Advanced features through Synapse Not supported in MAC", "review_text": "Synapse 4 currently does not support Razer Naga V3 Pro for MAC. This is ridiculous, and should be specified for buyers.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Jonny Quest", "review_title": "Sounds good on paper, BUT...", "review_text": "Pros: Swappable sides. Ring finger button (that you can disable when not needed!). Free spin mousewheel.
Cons: Oddly positioned two buttons added to left click side. Ring finger button/rest is insanely uncomfortable. Loud, tingy clicks. Plastic feels loose and cheap on the main click buttons.
I used the V2 and G600 for years. This seemed to be the best of both, but it didnt cut it for me. The clicks are intolerable. They have an annoying ting to them. After using this mouse for a couple of hours, the ring finger rest started to hurt. I noticed it's a very sharp design, that I just couldn't do. I still have my G600 and it's so much more comfortable. I really liked the free spin wheel. But, the V2 would let you actually adjust the mouse wheel to your liking instead of just 3 presets. Seems like a downgrade. Then there's the two new buttons that my fingers cant reach well, so what's the point? The plastic just also feels cheap and "creaky", which I never noticed on the V2. This ended up going back the next day. Bummer.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Adam", "review_title": "The New Hotness", "review_text": "Feels pretty much identical to the V2 Pro but it's far and away in my opinion the best MMO mouse available. The switches do feel ever so slightly better and the added buttons will be really nice for some users. Would recommend!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Cole", "review_title": "Good mouse design but questionable quality", "review_text": "The buttons on the 12 button MMO panel wobble and creak. They are not sturdy. The buttons on the bottom right of the panel are impossible to use without fat fingering an extra key.
I like the scroll wheel and the third click. The scroll wheel is three extra buttons on its own. The third click should probably be used infrequently as it is an unnatural hand gesture.
I’m coming from an old razer naga x with keys that don’t jiggle, more solid construction, all for a lower price. Doesn’t seem like there’s an equivalent to it these days. I wish they would make another dedicated 12 button and stop giving the mmo players this junk three panel nonsense.", "review_rating": ""}]

Title: Razer Viper V4 Pro Wireless Esports Gaming Mouse, 49g,180Hr Battery, Black
Description: 49G ULTRA LIGHTWEIGHT ESPORTS MOUSE — Built with input from competitive pro players, this wireless mouse is 9% lighter than the previous gen and delivers faster, more agile control for PC gaming
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Amazon Customer", "review_title": "The Ultimate Ambidextrous Endgame! 45 Days of Heavy Gaming and Pure Perfection", "review_text": "I am coming back to write this review after putting this mouse through its paces for a solid 45 days. After upgrading my desktop with a premium 8K magnetic keyboard, I knew my mouse setup had to match that elite level of performance. That is why I pulled the trigger on the latest Razer Viper V4 Pro, and after a month and a half of intense daily use, it has completely redefined my gaming experience. If you are looking for the absolute pinnacle of symmetrical gaming mice, this is the endgame.
First, let us talk about the design because there is a lot of confusion out there. This Viper V4 Pro is a flawless, perfectly symmetrical shape. It is a completely different beast compared to the older, bulky, asymmetrical right-handed design of the DeathAdder V4 Pro. As someone who prefers a claw/fingertip grip for high-precision micro-adjustments, this symmetrical shell melts into my hand perfectly, giving my thumb and fingers ultimate control.
At a mind-blowing 49 grams, the weight distribution is pure wizardry. Combined with the native 8000Hz polling rate and the 50K DPI sensor, the tracking feels like an extension of my own nervous system. In high-APM gaming sessions and chaotic shooters like World War Z or CS2, swapping targets is instantaneous with zero initial drag. Furthermore, it is an absolute dream for massive open-world action games like Where Winds Meet. During high-stakes martial arts combat, dodging, executing flawless parries, and rapidly controlling the 3D camera feels incredibly smooth and responsive. There is absolutely no pixel-skipping or camera stutter, giving me perfect situational awareness.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Krenzzler", "review_title": "This is just one of my favorite mice now", "review_text": "TLDR: This is the mouse I keep coming back to. Long story short, I want nothing more when using this mouse.
I'm one of those that just collects mice. I have my favorites, and I have some that I have just used once and put away. This is one that I keep bringing out. Simply put, the latest Viper and Deathadder are just some of my favorite mice period. They are built very solid, light weight, and flawless sensors. They have an instant wake up, fantastic battery life, satisfying clicks, great scroll wheel, and great side buttons. They are pricey, but quality-wise, it really doesn't get better than Razer now. And I'm comparing to Zowie, Logitech, G-wolves, Finalmouse, Pulsar, etc etc... Every one of those other brands has something I don't like in the quality alone, a creak, spongy click, or something keeps me from wanting to use those brands since I've used the Viper. Obviously, the shape is subjective, so if you've used the Viper V3 and didn't like the shape, you're not gonna like this. But I love the size shape, and weight. I can't wait to see the next Deathadder shed some weight to around 49g, and maybe implement some analog switches like the Logitech Superstrike. If they ever did that, I just hope they do weight balancing better because the superstrike is pretty front heavy, but I'm perfectly happy with Razer's optical switches because they just feel sooooo good. But I think the haptic analog switches would be very interesting in the Deathadder shape. I really don't know how they could improve on this other than finding more ways to lighten the weight even more. Razer might've perfected the Viper with this iteration.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Dylan", "review_title": "Great Gaming Mouse for 2026", "review_text": "This is the best gaming mouse as someone who upgraded from a regular stock mouse. The weight, the functionality, and the design of the mouse is perfect. In fact, this mouse, and it features had further fine-tuned my already decent aim. After using this mouse for a while, I have observed my aim became a natural aim bot, where I was even accused of potentially exploiting in a match of BF1.
The mouse itself is light, and as someone who came from a heavier mouse it felt a bit weird at first. However, if you can manage it, then it becomes a benefit. It allows you to flick quickly, and track targets consistently, which is where my claim of "natural aim bot" came from. It's not too light where you might find yourself tensing up too much to keep it in place, but if you came from a heavier mouse, then you might overflick your target a few times.
The features the mouse offered through Razer's Synapse software such as the DPI and mappings are very useful. You can set different profiles for different games, so there are different DPI's for each game. In addition, you can change the mouse's buttons to be mapped to keys on your keyboard. For example, you can have the side button mapped to 'R', so you can reload through the side button. You can also have the same side buttons run a macro, so if you're playing Helldivers 2, you can instantly input a stratagem through your side button. There are also features like letting the side buttons launch a program.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Kayne P", "review_title": "The perfect mouse?", "review_text": "I don’t typically write reviews, but this mouse is hands down the best I’ve ever had the pleasure of using, so I feel like I must. The moment my hand gripped the mouse, I knew it was the one. The build quality is fantastic. Everything. From the clicks to the sensor, the scroll wheel and the side buttons. Everything is perfect. The coating on the mouse is high quality and the dongle that comes with it is nicely weighted so it doesn’t slip around on your desk. The stock skates are also wonderful and glide around on my Artisan Zero Soft so smoothly. The size and shape is perfect for my grip style (relaxed claw) so I can handle it comfortably. I recently just bought a GPX Superlight 2 as well as an X2 Crazylight Medium and neither felt quite right. So I decided to try this mouse and it did everything for me the other two couldn’t. Since I bought the Razer Viper V4 Pro, I’ve seen a massive improvement in my gameplay. And for that reason I can confidently justify the price of this product. 5 Stars. Genuinely amazing product across the board. Dare I say perfect. 👍 ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Anthony", "review_title": "Left me Surprised in a Good Way", "review_text": "This mouse took me by surprise.
Coming from the Basilisk V3 Pro, this one is just so lightweight that I almost mistook it for a toy. I seriously can't believe how light this is.
The battery life is phenomenal, and the controls are astoundingly tight. The buttons on my Basilisk always felt cheap and mushy, but every button on this Viper V4 Pro is snappy and solid.
Getting to the part people care about most, this is probably the most fluid mouse I've ever used. The 50K sensor is a marketing ploy, as I don't use anything over 6400DPI, but you can turn on the 8K polling with a high refresh rate monitor and you won't see any dragging of your cursor across your screen as you will with lower refresh rates, and the higher polling rate shows your mouse's location on the screen more times per second than traditional 1K polling rates. My eyes can see the difference, but only if I strain to see it.
I run the mouse at 1K polling rate for optimal battery life and because most games are using that rate the most effectively. It's a sweet spot.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Charles myers", "review_title": "Is it worth the upgrade?", "review_text": "The Razer Viper V4 Pro is a flagship-level esports mouse that doubles down on performance rather than reinventing the formula. It features an ultra-lightweight ambidextrous design at around 49–50g, paired with Razer’s Focus Pro 50K optical sensor capable of 50,000 DPI, 930 IPS tracking, and 90G acceleration. It also introduces Gen-4 optical switches, improved wireless performance with an upgraded dongle, and up to 180 hours of battery life. On paper, it’s one of the most technically refined mice available fast, consistent, and clearly built for competitive play.
That said, if you already own the Razer Viper V3 Pro, there’s honestly no real reason to upgrade. The improvements here are incremental slightly better battery life, marginally upgraded switches, and small refinements that you’re not going to feel in-game. The V3 Pro is already insanely lightweight, responsive, and accurate, so the V4 Pro ends up feeling more like a spec bump than a meaningful evolution. Unless you’re chasing absolute top-end specs for the sake of it, you’re better off sticking with the V3 Pro. As a stand alone mouse, I give it 4 stars. As a "upgrade" to the previous generation I'd give it one star.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Marco", "review_title": "New main. Excellent mouse with a ridiculous battery life", "review_text": "The box didn't have much protection, but it arrived in great condition. As for the mouse itself, it is amazing.
I won't talk much about shape because that's highly subjective (I'll just say it fits my hand size and grip style), but everything else is excellent: coating is smooth and grippy, very nice to the touch; main clicks are light and tactile, tho they could have a little less post travel; side buttons are well tensioned and positioned; the wheel might be the weakest aspect, because the scrolling feels a bit off, but it's totally functional; M3 click is very tactile; skates are smooth and fast; build quality is perfect, solid as a rock; performance is top tier, no complaints; and finally, the battery is absolutely insane. I have been using the mouse for 12 days at 1000hz (sometimes 8000, but only for a couple of Apex matches) and it has only gone down to 60%.
On top of all of that, Razer has finally made a web software. That means 2 things: 1) you don't have to deal with the bloatware that is Synapse (except for firmware updates); and 2) you can change your settings on Linux, which has been a game changer for me (I dual boot Windows 11 and Bazzite).
I think it is worth the price, but only if you don't have a Viper V3 Pro (or even a Viper V3 Pro SE). On paper, the V4 Pro has many improvements, but the only real upgrade that a player will notice is the battery life and the web software. I recommend it to people who have never owned a Viper V3 and want the latest technology and power efficiency. I can recommend it to those who just want to try the shape, but they might also want to take a look at the V3 Pro, since it is cheaper right now.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Nick", "review_title": "Worthy of the praise", "review_text": "I have been using it a full week now, and I think it's worth all the praise. It's a safe shape that will work for everyone except if your hands are on the smaller side. Switches, side buttons, scroll wheel, and sensor all feel perfect. My honest favorite thing about this mouse is the battery life is otherworldly good compared to anything I have used. I likely won't have to charge it until about 5-6 weeks of moderate to heavy use at 1000Hz, which is huge when I need to charge my other mice practically after a weekend.
The first negative is the price is steep, especially when you could get the V3 Pro Se for like have the price. Two, the M1/M2 switches are on the loud side, but you won't notice them with headphones. You will annoy anyone around you though if they have to listen to you click. Three, the black version is a bit of an oil magnet, but the coating at least feels good. Might be worth using either Razer's provided grips or another brands for long-term use.
Overall, it's a very good mouse if it's within your price range, and your hands are moderately large in size. Maybe it's placebo, but I also dropped my first nuke in Call of Duty on keyboard and mouse using it. That might be influencing might personal opinion of it, but I promise it's a great mouse.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Ramz1333", "review_title": "ممتاز جداً", "review_text": "رهيبه بس صوت الازرار عالي جداً", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Sebin jose", "review_title": "Best mouse for competitive games", "review_text": "Best in the market. As always razerr", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Luca Preda", "review_title": "Great all around mouse", "review_text": "I would argue this mouse is better than the superstrike 2 in the way a porsche 911 drives, it just does what you want. I’ve had zero issues, just a lightweight, easy to use mouse that works well on both cloth and glass mousepads. 49g seems like the perfect weight before getting too light for me, and it suits all three grip types well. Battery is genuinely insane, I can charge it fully and leave it at 2000hz polling rate for a month and a half of daily use (multiple hours) before I need to charge it again. The web software is reasonably clear and has good features too, letting you change things like liftoff distance, mouse tilt angle and so on.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Saleh Gharaibeh", "review_title": "Perfect.", "review_text": "Lightweight, responsive, all you can ask from a gaming mouse. The skates feel really decent just be sure and remove the very fine plastic covering from them like i didn't for the first week (they were hard to see & i didn't know they were on) I really enjoyed using this mouse because despite the click latency which really isn't a big deal unless your competing, the mouse performs amicably.
