Title: Razer Viper V3 Pro Wireless Esports Gaming Mouse, 54g Lightweight, Black
Description: 54 G ULTRA LIGHTWEIGHT DESIGN — Designed in collaboration with world-class esports pros, the Viper V3 Pro’s perfectly balanced ultra lightweight design allows gamers to make swift, precise flicks that match every intention
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Chanly Duong", "review_title": "my review of the razor viper v3 pro", "review_text": "now for my background, i play r6 and csgo, and occasionally roblox shooters. i went from originally a 60g razer orochi v2 using a fingertip grip, and i went to this mouse with a traditional claw. i’ve had this mouse for a few months and i can say that this is a very good and universal shape for all sorts of grips. i have a medium size hand and i can comfortably fingertip and claw this mouse.
the coating is lovely and the best i’ve personally felt on a mouse, and i tried the grips but they eventually wear out over time so i don’t recommend using those (the actual mouse texture is better than the grips anyway). now i know this sounds a little ridiculous but moving from a 60g small mouse not even including the batteries, i played a LOT better with this bigger one after adjusting and i’m honestly happy with my purchase (even though it cost quite a bit). it feels light in the hand for the size and the weight is flawlessly distributed. the skates are solid for being stock but you can always upgrade, the scroll wheel is pretty normal and has distinctive bumps per scroll but personally i like more smoother ones (i am probably just being nitpicky). the main clicks are lovely to hear and the little dongle included doesn’t take up too much space, i’d say only the actual cable itself does but this isn’t actually an issue. the dongle can also support up to 8k hz which isn’t necessary but it’s a “nice to have” feature and i use 2k hz myself to save battery life;", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "CyndiCat", "review_title": "Highly recommend for competitive gamers.", "review_text": "(Review from my 15 year old son)
Honestly this mouse felt SO much lighter than I thought it would. I just upgraded from the Glorious Model O- Wireless Gaming Mouse, and let me say... the upgrade was WORTH it for sure. I pretty much only play Fortnite on Keyboard and Mouse, and I was having issues with my side buttons on my old mouse. I decided it was time to upgrade since I can't have those issues happening mid-game. The Razer Viper V3 Pro, is definitely a solid upgrade. The side buttons are so much more solid than the side buttons on my old mouse. Not to mention, the response time of the clicks was faster, and the accuracy of my aim with the better sensor was so much better. The scroll wheel is also very responsive and fast which is important for Fortnite. (I was able to easily quad edit in Fortnite when using this new mouse)
The wireless connectivity isn't even noticeable at all. The response time is insane for a wireless mouse, and it surprised me a lot. I don't have a lot to say about the battery life yet, as this is my first day using it. I will say though, I charged the mouse to 68%, used it for an hour in Fortnite, and the battery was only 67% afterwards.
Here are the few cons I can think of:", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "yandre", "review_title": "Expensive, but great mouse.", "review_text": "The Razer Viper V3 has been an excellent mouse for both gaming and everyday use. It feels very lightweight and comfortable in hand, making long sessions easy with no fatigue. The shape is simple but very ergonomic, and it works well for both claw and fingertip grip styles.
Performance wise, the sensor is extremely accurate and responsive. Tracking is smooth, clicks feel crisp, and there is no noticeable delay. The wireless connection is stable and reliable, with no lag or dropouts. Battery life has also been great, lasting several days of heavy use without needing frequent charging.
Build quality feels solid, and the mouse buttons and scroll wheel all feel well made. Overall, the Viper V3 delivers excellent performance, comfort, and reliability. It is a great choice for anyone looking for a high quality lightweight gaming mouse.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Danny", "review_title": "Good claw grip mouse", "review_text": "I had a Logitech superlight and moved to the Viper v3 pro. It was the best decision that I have ever made. The mouse sensor in my opinion is more accurate the Logitech mice. The feel and texture and material of the mouse feels very nice especially the white coating option is phenomenal and has really good grip for a very low amount of weight gain. The size definitely favors mid-big hands and excels in the Claw grip. It isn't the lightest mouse on the market but it still in my opinion is more than light enough for most. The scroll wheel actually feels quite nice and i prefer it over the Logitech one. Though this mouse supports 8k polling I rarely find myself using it as it drains battery too fast, I would just use 4000/2000 if you want a high enough speed with a very long battery life. If you are looking for a high quality claw grip mouse then this is the mouse for you, if you don't have a claw grip I would recommend looking at other mice that might be for you.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "The Lovely Lyss", "review_title": "Most satisfying mouse I have ever used; full stop.", "review_text": "As someone who loves the Superlight and has been jamming out with version 2 of it along with a Logitech Pro X TKL paired with it, it's been nice to swap back to my Black Widow V4 along with the Viper Pro 3.
Right out of the box, and I am someone with medium to large hands, this mouse is just a pure delight to hold; it's not often I can say that my hands feel like they disappear when using a peripheral, but this mouse and the Superlight from Logi are the two mice that achieve that for me. Razer knew what they were doing here and it shows in the product; this will be my go-to mouse and I will alternate my Razer setup back to the Logitech set up as the mood strikes me to change things up week by week.
When it comes time for the Wooting 80HE to arrive, I will most likely be pairing the Viper Pro 3 with that board due to just how consistently good it feels; I am 3 hours deep into a play session and the battery is down to 98% and I'm using the 4K polling rate; not going to bother with 8K just yet.
It's hard to put into words here just how good the slight ergo shape of this mouse feels; I really have tried a number of different mice and this could be "the one"; I don't say this in a hyperbolic fashion either. It's rare that you use a gaming device where you just forget what you're using because it seamlessly blends into the play session.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "R", "review_title": "Surprisingly lightweight, good polling rate and no wifi-interference!", "review_text": "So far so good. I was impressed on how light this mouse felt when I used it for the first time. You can definitely feel the extra accuracy when you aim, by that I mean every small movement you make on your mousepad translates exactly as you would expect on the screen. My router and modem are right under my desk and I don't get any interference. I don't open the program that comes with it (synapse) because I used a wired headset with it (razer blackshark v2 X) and I don't want synapse messing the audio settings of my headset since the default option is pretty good. The battery works for a long time; I used it for like 3 consecutive days and when I open synapse to check battery is about 70% (I use 2k polling rate). Clicking sounds satisfying as you would expect from an expensive mouse. Your forearm gets considerably less tired. The side buttons and click buttons have not collected any dust or grime from my hands, unlike my old mouse did.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Steven", "review_title": "Light with great battery life", "review_text": "I have had this mouse for about a year now and use it as my daily driver, and I love it.
It is really light and glides across the mouse pad. The mouse wheel is not noisy at all and neither is the clicking of the mouse buttons imo. The battery life is good lasting more than a few all day play sessions, and a couple of weeks of light use.
It comes with some little adhesive pads that you can place on the mouse which I would recommend using as the mouse is very smooth.
My complaints are that the mouse gets clammy feeling after a while. Not a huge deal, but I have thought of buying another adhesive pad to go over the emblem because it gets to feel gross. I do clean it, but this is the only mouse I have ever had this issue with. Also the dongle is kind of a pain if you have OCD, it is hard to get it to lay flat down.
Overall I love the mouse and think it is worth the money. I would just recommend buying an adhesive patch (I'm not sure what they are really called) to go over the razer emblem as that part can start to feel gross.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Krave", "review_title": "Amazing for FPS", "review_text": "This is by far the best mouse I’ve ever owned, and I’ve owned several, including the Razer DeathAdder, Mamba, Mamba Elite, and most recently, the SteelSeries Aerox 5 Wireless. I switched to this mouse because the scroll wheel on the Aerox breaks far too quickly. Initially, I was hesitant to get the Viper due to the Aerox 5's five side buttons but I’m so glad I made the switch!
This mouse is incredible. The response speeds are super fast, it’s insanely light, and it glides effortlessly across my mouse pad. The battery life is also outstanding. I used it for four days straight before putting it on the charger as I was going to bed, and it still had 37% left. Switching between wired and wireless modes is instant, which is a huge improvement over my Aerox 5, where connections sometimes took minutes. The scroll wheel feels high quality and has deep notches.
I’m not sure why I see people hating on Razer Synapse. Maybe I'm a little biased since I've always used razer keyboards, and am Using the Huntsman pro rn but I've never had issue and I always found it pretty convenient for making macros and chroma effects and the features Synapse has for this mouse is pretty Dope. For example, you can create your own sensitivity response curve, similar to how controller settings work in many games. Additionally, if you grip your mouse at an angle, as I do with a left leaning grip, you can tell Synapse your grip style using a slider for better horizontal accuracy. You can also have synapse auto switch polling rates depending on if your in a fullscreen game or just browsing the web which makes the battery last ages. I use 2000hz in-game and 1000hz out.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Oswar", "review_title": "Very nice", "review_text": "Very nice", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Rodrigo Guimarães de Souza", "review_title": "Recomendo", "review_text": "Produto original! Novo! Produto chegou com mais de 15 dias de antecedência da previsão inicial!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Mohammad aljasir", "review_title": "Super comfortable", "review_text": "Light and feel nice", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Mauricio", "review_title": "Recomendado", "review_text": "Extremadamente ligero y con bateria duradera, muy buen mouse… super recomendado", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Amazon Customer", "review_title": "Highly recommend great mouse", "review_text": "Great mouse but higher polling rates affect fps depending on your pc", "review_rating": ""}]

Title: Logitech G PRO X Superlight 2 Wireless Gaming Mouse - Black
Description: Better Performance: The Logitech Superlight 2, our championship winning wireless mouse gaming is now even better; with 8 kHz polling, USB-C charging, 95-hour battery life and POWERPLAY compatibility at 60 g
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Iggy Gonzalez", "review_title": "Lightweight, Fast, and Worth It", "review_text": "The G PRO X Superlight 2 is an excellent gaming mouse. It’s incredibly lightweight, tracks flawlessly, and feels very responsive in fast-paced games. The battery life is great, the shape is comfortable for long sessions, and the build quality feels premium. It’s expensive, but if you’re serious about gaming, it’s absolutely worth the investment.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Julia", "review_title": "Crazy light and perfect for gaming", "review_text": "I have been using this mouse for a couple weeks now and honestly it has been amazing. The first thing you notice is how light it is. It almost feels like nothing in your hand which made a huge difference for me in FPS games and even just normal computer use. My aim feels smoother and my wrist does not get tired after long sessions. As someone who games in the mornings before studying or rotations, it has been a really nice upgrade.
The clicks feel super crisp and responsive and the wireless connection has been flawless so far. No lag, no random disconnects, and the battery life has been better than I expected. The shape is comfortable even after hours of use and it fits well for both claw and palm grip. Setup was simple and the software was easy to use to adjust DPI and buttons.
Overall this is easily one of the best mice I have owned. It feels premium, performs great, and actually made gaming more enjoyable for me. If you are thinking about upgrading your mouse, especially for competitive games, I would definitely recommend this one.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Will Miles", "review_title": "Excellent Mouse for Competitive Gaming", "review_text": "The Superlight 2 has easily become one of my favorite gaming mice. The first thing you notice is how light it is. At around 60g, movements feel incredibly quick and effortless, which has been especially noticeable for me in FPS games where fast flicks and precise adjustments matter.
Tracking feels extremely accurate and consistent, and wireless performance has been flawless. I haven’t noticed any input delay compared to a wired mouse. Battery life is also excellent—I can use it for long gaming sessions without constantly thinking about charging it.
I also really like the shape. It’s simple, comfortable, and doesn’t try to do anything weird ergonomically, so it works well for both gaming and everyday PC use. The white version looks especially clean paired with a white setup.
It’s definitely expensive for a mouse, but you’re paying for the extremely low weight, excellent sensor, reliable wireless connection, and overall refinement. If competitive FPS games are a big part of what you play, the Superlight 2 absolutely lives up to its reputation.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Damian Pizarro", "review_title": "Crisp, Precise, and Worth Every Dollar!!", "review_text": "The Logitech G Pro X Superlight 2 is easily one of the best mice I’ve used. It’s extremely light without feeling cheap, and the sensor performance is outstanding. When paired with a glass mouse pad, the glide is insanely smooth and tracking feels incredibly clean and precise.
Because I have larger hands, I added grip tape and highly recommend it for anyone in the same boat. Without grip tape I had to grip the mouse tighter than I liked, but with it, control and comfort improved immediately. Combined with the crisp clicks, reliable wireless performance, and long battery life, this mouse delivers exactly what it promises. Pricey, but well worth it.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Why do you need to know ts?", "review_title": "Really Good All Around", "review_text": "Good ergonomics, nice and light, glides well, good software, battery lasts a long time.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Star", "review_title": "Lightweight gaming mouse. Mouse size is decent for small hands.", "review_text": "Been using this mouse for about 6 months for work, school, and gaming. The mouse size is alright. I have small hands, and my hand doesn't get sore or strained using it for several hours. It has decent ergonomics. The clicks are much quieter than a Razer Viper V3 Pro. The sound clicks are as "loud" as linear switches (which are fairly quiet) if noise level is a concern for you. I prefer quieter, but tactile clicks, which this mouse does quite nicely. The mouse clicks don't bother me when I'm working at night.
Battery life lasts quite a long time for this mouse. I can use this mouse for a couple of days (or even a week, if I'm taking breaks) without having to charge it. On Logitech G HUB, it says the battery life lasts for approximately 96 hours. You'd have to download Logitech G HUB to customize macros and set sensitivity on the mouse. If you're using this mouse for mainly gaming, make sure to go to "Device Settings" and under "Lightforce Switch" set it to "Optical Only". This will decrease battery life, but will utilize the full performance of the optical switch and has lower latency.
My only gripes are the Logitech G HUB is glitchy sometimes and certain game profiles don't automatically switch over, like when I tab in and out between the desktop and Fortnite, and the software doesn't automatically switch to the "Fortnite" profile, and the side buttons feel a bit mushy when building and editing in Fortnite. The side buttons could be a bit crispier.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Tildon M.", "review_title": "Pretty Sweet Gaming Mouse", "review_text": "I've had it for 4 1/2 months now, great feeling mouse, very responsive and fast, it looks sick in my setup, and I've only had to charge it about 2 times since I got it so good battery life. Having to download G Hub to configure it for the first time I'd say was fairly easy but I recommend configuring it, turning on on board memory mode, and forgetting the software. Also about 3 months into having it I spilled a whole cup of water on it and spent like 20 minutes getting all the liquid out of the mouse and a month later it still works like it's brand new lol.
For the price, I'd only recommend it to some, but overall pretty sweet mouse.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Derek", "review_title": "Logitech still hasn't gotten their quality control in line over the last 6 years of making mice.", "review_text": "About 6 years ago I bought a g pro wireless, the first one had an issue with double clicking with the primary left click AND the middle click. That developed after ~4-7 days of use. Logitech RMA'd it and sent me a new mouse. This second mouse immediately had issues with the left click where it was mushy and had significant travel past the actual click sound. They RMA'd this one too. Finally by the third mouse I got one that worked good, no double clicking, no middle mouse button issues..... for maybe 2.5 years. 0.5 years past the warranty period. I lived with the mouse button issues for a while until it became unbearable to the point where I can't reliably move the camera anymore in league of legends, or rotate the camera in many 3rd person games/3d software. I decided to get this mouse (G PRO X SUPERLIGHT 2) to replace the aged g pro wireless. It seems logitech has learned absolutely nothing in their quality control department over the years. This mouse that I just got ALREADY has scroll wheel decoder issues where it scrolls in the opposite direction briefly before scrolling in the correct direction. Secondly, it has a squealing noise as a scroll upwards that is already unbearable to listen to. I've had enough of logitech mice. I hate the situation because I love the G pro's shape and feel. The silver lining is that there are MANY competing mice now that offer great performance for less, or about the same amount of money which copied the shape and feel. This will likely be the last logitech mouse I buy and am returning it. Razer Viper V3 pro here I come.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Ivan Guerrero Azamar", "review_title": "Resistente", "review_text": "El mouse se siente mas robusto que el G Pro Superlight al igual que sus clicks pero eso mismo hace que el mouses aguante mas y apesar de que es mas robusto pesa menos que el anterior, es una compra totalmente recomendable si es que quieres un mouse que los clicks duren mucho, que sea comodo y pesando casi nada", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "AC", "review_title": "Great for fps, ok for work, same issues as other mice", "review_text": "Using this for work and various video games (cs). Very light mouse, almost feels like air. Build quality is excellent, the materials are pleasant to the touch. The sensor is very precise and smooth, this mouse wont let you down in a clutch. No issues with battery life (multiple full days), just keep a usb-c cable nearby. My phone charger is multipurpose now, phone/headset/mouse.
The only issue is the middle click (mouse3): when held down, it can register multiple clicks when slightly changing pressure. For gaming, no big deal; for working, very lame (can close/open multiple tabs by accident). From forums/reddit, this is common to most (if not all) superlights.
I've used the superlight for several months now with no new issues (other than the middle button).
Before this, I've had at least seven wired and later wireless g703s. Something usually breaks within a year or so (left/right double clicking, mouse wheel issues, etc.). I expect the same for the superlight. That's gaming, cant help it. Might sound bad, but both g703 and superlight are excellent mice. With heavy use, it is inevitable that something breaks eventually. If looking for cheaper mice, g703 is a heavier alternative.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "S.Almheiri", "review_title": "Logitech G PRO X Superlight 2", "review_text": "I have tried various types of gaming mouse set-ups and I have found this mouse to be almost perfect from the ergonomics, battery life, charging, and practicality. I have been using it for a couple of months for various tasks such as work, studies, gaming, and general use. Currently I have no complaints other than that price is high. Finally what made buy this version compared to the superlight 1 is the type-c charger which is worth it.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Kauan Veras", "review_title": "Excelente Mouse", "review_text": "Muito bom chegou em perfeito estado e gostei muito do mouse", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Jehiel George", "review_title": "Solid Mouse, But Time for a Price Drop", "review_text": "I got the G PRO X SUPERLIGHT 2, and it's pretty great. First off it's insanely lightweight, which is a great touch if you're into quick movements. Feels good in the hand and is super responsive. The battery life is solid too, it holds charge for a decent amount of time, and when you do need to charge it, it's fast. Build quality seems sturdy, like it won’t just fall apart if you’re a bit rough with it.
That said, for how good it is, there are a lot of other mice out there offering similar stuff at cheaper prices now. I still like it, but honestly, it might be time for Logitech to consider bringing the price down a notch with all the competition around. It’s still worth it, just... a little less of a splurge would be nice.", "review_rating": ""}]

Title: GravaStar Mercury X Pro Wireless Gaming Mouse, Come with 8K Dongle – 32,000 DPI PAW 3950 Sensor, 8,000Hz Polling Rate, Only 49g, Magnesium Alloy Hollow Frame, RGB Lighting, 5 Programmable Buttons
Description: Innovative Hollow Skeleton Design - Maximized airflow with a durable, lightweight magnesium alloy frame to keep your hand cool and dry during intense gaming sessions.
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Steven", "review_title": "Very Cool, but does have a premium price for the extra coolness", "review_text": "It has been a long time in the accessory space since a company came out with products that were different and unique but didn't also stink at the function that they are supposed to perform. This is not one of them. Like their keyboards, GravaStar has made this crazy looking mouse that is actually an excellent gaming mouse. (Or just mouse in general.)
It is a premium product at a premium price so I do have a few nitpicks, but overall it is an excellent mouse.
Taking it out of the box, and it is both very light but also feels premium. Squeezing it much harder then I should and it is very rigid and strong. The web based configuration is okay. Since I have one of their keyboards and the software that comes with that I think it would be nice if that was integrated into one system. Otherwise it is nice to be able to fine tune the sensitivity and even though I had no issue with debounce (clicking once and sometimes getting double clicks) but it is nice to be able to adjust that. And finally something that I never thought I would say... I like the RGB. In generally it just seems sort of silly to have RGB on a mouse, but this one makes it work and adds to the whole vibe, especially when paired with one of their keyboards.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Mustang GT", "review_title": "My favorite gaming mouse I've ever owned", "review_text": "I've used quite a few gaming mice over the years, and this is easily my favorite. I'm a huge GravaStar fan, and this mouse absolutely lives up to the hype. I mainly play Apex Legends, Call of Duty, and Fortnite, and the accuracy and responsiveness are insane. It feels incredibly precise, making quick movements and tracking feel effortless.
One of my favorite features is how customizable everything is. After downloading the software, you can adjust the polling rate, DPI, RGB lighting, button functions, and even the breathing effects for the lighting. It's easy to use and gives you complete control over how you want the mouse to perform and look.
The lightweight design is also extremely comfortable during long gaming sessions without sacrificing durability. For me, this mouse has been worth every penny. If you're looking for a premium gaming mouse with excellent performance and endless customization, I highly recommend giving this one a try. This is a mouse that will last you forever and thats why I bought it.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Brittany Lammers", "review_title": "Great fancy mouse", "review_text": "Really nice mouse. I love the look of it. Love how Alien type looks, my hand is really small and have palm rest on it and i love all of it!. I was scared at first that would be too big, but nope fits perfectly for small hands, it feel sturdy and very light. So far it have lasted great I will update if something happens, the battery life is great i'm someone that love have the lights on all the time and always forgets to charge their mouse. I could be more than 3 days with 8+ hours play time and it last for long.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Alfredo", "review_title": "Sick high quality", "review_text": "Excellent item, I’m coming from a Logitech g502 pro wireless that is a pretty heavy one, I use it for play fps games and I have to say it works perfectly. I play full hand so I was worried about the size before get this one but I have to say that for the minimum weight, it has a pretty decent size that feels great in the hand. You can feel the high quality there and the software is pretty easy to use. And also looks sick. Great value if you constantly play and want something of quality", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Claudia Lacosta", "review_title": "Buy it!", "review_text": "Hands down it’s worth every penny. It’s pricey but love it, don’t cheap out. Light weight & fast.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Michael Berry", "review_title": "From a mouse junkie... Nearly Perfect", "review_text": "I was pleasantly surprised by the Gravastar Mercury X Pro... This mouse is really great and has the features we're all looking for (3950 sensor, 8k polling rate, adjustable LOD, motion sync) all wrapped up in a downloadable OR web interface. I love having the choice - you can configure the mouse via webpage, or via the software to download.
The RGB is great. I usually don't pick mice with it, I go for the $100-150 class mouse (I have around 10 of them, too). This mouse is definitely up there in the quality department, it feels just as nice as my other $170 magnesium mouse. The look is stunning and unique, I love the default colorway and it really stands out. It's a pleasure to use, except...
Side slits :( Side slits :( Side slits :(... this is the only thing preventing me from giving it 5 stars. Your thumb and ring/pinkie fingers on the side of the mouse will be holding slits. Title: Rosonway 7 Ports Powered USB 3.2/USB C Hub 10Gbps with 4 USB-C 3.2, 3 USB-A 3.2 Ports, 3.3ft Cable and 36W(12V/3A) Power Adapter, Aluminum USB Splitter for Laptop, RSH-H7C4
Description: Hybrid USB Port Expander: Rosonway 7 Ports Powered USB hub with 4 USB-C 3.2 ports and 3 USB-A 3.2 ports, allowing you to easily connect to your laptop, desktop, gaming console, and more—transforming a single port into a complete workstation. Plug-and-play, no drivers required. Simplify your setup and boost productivity
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "John Caravaggio", "review_title": "Do you have an external drive that has a short cable?", "review_text": "I have a LITE-ON USB 2.0 External CD/DVD Writer Model eUAU108, manufactured in 2013, with an attached cable that is slightly less than 4 inches long. This model was an improvement over prior models, in that it requires only a single USB 2.0 connection, whereas previous models employed a Y-cable to enable connecting to 2 USB ports simultaneously for additional power. I have always felt that this drive was marginally capable of running on the 500 mA specification for USB 2.0 ports. I think this is the main reason for the ultra short cable - to minimize the voltage drop.
The short cable worked OK when I was using the drive with a laptop, but attempting to use it with a computer attached to the back of my flat screen monitor is a major problem. The USB ports are about a foot above the desktop, making it necessary to support the drive in some manner. This has always been problematic. I tried using the only USB extension cable that I had, a cheap dollar store cable, and it did not work at all.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Amazon Customer", "review_title": "Great Hub, Great Value!", "review_text": "Review of Rosonway 7 Ports USB 3.2 Hub 36W
I purchased the Rosonway 7 Ports USB 3.2 Hub 36W and tested it in two separate configurations. First with my Surface PC laptop operating Windows and second with my Mac Mini 4 operating Sequoia. The Hub, which is powered with a 36W(12V/3A) DC power adapter, comes with 7 Ports, 4 USB-C 3.2 ports and 3 USB-A 3.2 ports. It claims speeds up to 10Gbps on every port.
The Hub is small and sturdy aluminum device with independent electronic switches on each port and a blue LED indicator to display power status. This enables power management over all connected devices. When I connected it to my Surface laptop PC it worked seamlessly. I was able to connect to my external mouse and keyboard, 4 thumb drives and an external backup drive. The computer recognized all the drives and could rapidly access the external backup even with all these peripherals attached and running, the hub did not get hot (only warm as would be expected).", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Hajster", "review_title": "Awesome 1-Stop Solution for Travel Power and Data Connectivity!", "review_text": "This device is the perfect accessory for someone needing to connect multiple devices using a single interface. Excellent for traveling light, I'm looking forward to my next trip with the need for only this charging / data hub and my laptop. Not only does this hub provide connectivity for both USB A and USB C connections, allowing me to pass data seamlessly between all of my devices without a need to repeated disconnect / reconnect for access to ports, it also CHARGES all of them simultaneously using the included 36W power supply.
It was incredibly easy to decide which devices to activate with individual power switches for each port and indicators to show which ones are active. I did NOT need to deactivate any of the ports, however, as there was ample power to charge all of my equipment at one time. That means a lot when I'm traveling with early morning departures and late arrivals each day, giving me a single place to charge everything at once while I sleep and wake up ready for the next adventure.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "william", "review_title": "Solid powered USB hub that has performed in the time I have used it.", "review_text": "I have been in IT long enough to know that a USB hub is one of those products that sounds simple on paper but has a surprisingly wide range of quality in practice. I have also been burned enough times by bad ones to approach any new hub with a healthy dose of skepticism. So when I say that the Rosonway powered USB hub has genuinely impressed me, I want you to understand that it is coming from someone who does not hand out compliments to peripheral hardware easily.
I have had this hub for 13 days now. That might not sound like a long time, but in the context of my daily IT work, I have put it through what I would consider a serious run of testing. This is not a hub that has been sitting on a desk powering a wireless mouse dongle and a phone charger. It has been put through a ringer of a minimum of 12-14 hours 5-6 days a week. And it was used every day. With a rotating cast of demanding devices that would expose any weakness in a lesser product.
Why I Came Back to Rosonway
This is actually my second Rosonway hub. My first one is still running, still reliable, and was purchased specifically because I had grown so frustrated with other brands that I needed something I could actually count on. Before finding Rosonway the first time, I dealt with pretty much every problem a USB hub can throw at you — and often all at once. Devices dropping connection randomly. Transfer speeds that had no business being as slow as they were, even on a nominally high-speed hub. Units that died within weeks of purchase. Build quality that felt like it might give out at any moment.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Andrew", "review_title": "Reliable, well‑built 7-port USB 3.2 hub", "review_text": "TLDR: This is a fast, powerful, versatile 7-port USB 3.2 Gbps hub that gives you lots of ports which is especially useful for modern laptops which often only have one port.
This connects to a laptop/PC via a USB-C cable. It also needs a power cable to function so make sure you are close to a wall outlet or even better, a surge protector.
You get 7 ports - 4 USB-C ports and 3 classic USB-A ports. They are all version 3.2 ports with a speeds up to 10Gbps. You can toggle each one on/off with the buttons on the side. The ports have a light that comes on with enabled.
It's got sturdy aluminum body so it's safe to transport and won't get damaged in your backpack.
Performance‑wise, it’s handled everything I’ve thrown at it. I’ve had multiple drives, a mouse, a keyboard, and a couple of random accessories plugged in at the same time, and it didn’t choke or overheat — just got slightly warm, which is normal. The 10Gbps ports definitely move files quickly, and the external power supply keeps everything stable. It’s not meant to fast‑charge big devices, but for data and powering smaller gear, it’s been rock‑steady.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Rob Holmes", "review_title": "Well made and as fast as native computer USB ports.", "review_text": "Rosonway 7 Ports Powered USB 3.2/USB C Hub RSH-H7C4
This a really compact and robust feeling device. It is attractive with polished chrome accents against a matte black finish, so it doesn’t fingerprint. The size a small enough to easily fit in my modest laptop bag. It’s small for having so many ports, about the size of a small remote control. The USB cable is thick and feels like it’s designed to carry the throughput it’s intended too. I found no difference between transfer speeds of a hard drive compared to it plugged directly into my computer.
1. External Mechanical Hard Drive Throughput: See attachment.
2. Good packaging
3. The cords aligned with the length coming out the back make it easy to put anywhere. The ports on top make it easy to put in tight spaces. Similar products with the ports on the sides/edges make it difficult to put in tight spaces on small work surfaces
4. SD Card reader used in the device: 92mb – 165mb/s (In computer: 91-167mb/s)", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "1st2Summit", "review_title": "Great UBS hub to expand you ports", "review_text": "My work laptop only has 2 USB-As and 1 USB-C ports and BT is disabled and I need to connect more devices than available ports. So I'm using this to connect my wireless keyboard and mouse, speaker, ring light, and a 2.5Gbps ethernet adapter. It's got 4 USB-C and 3 USB-A plugs so you have your choice of connections. It's compact and the cables are long enough to reach the outlet on the floor. I like the buttons have an audible and tactile click to turn on and does require a long-press to turn off so it doesn't accidentally disconnect a device - something that does happen to one of my other USB hubs.
The body is aluminum so it's got a solid feel and the cables are thick and solid so I think it will last a while for travel.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Russ Grasso", "review_title": "Quality & design issues surfaced during usage", "review_text": "August 2023 update: On the 3rd week, my 2nd unit started to blink two hard drive connections on and off with only 3 ports switched on. Therefore rating is reduced to 1 star from 2.
Initially, my 2nd unit successfully wrote 350 Gb drive to drive across this hub without any buffering errors (buffering errors are what usually goes wrong in such tests). Speed was about 40 - 70 mb per second for nominally-sized files. However was unable to complete a chkdsk on a mounted drive without terminating in a unidentifiable error (again usually what happens with bad hubs).
My first unit which was returned had a bad port #3 (counting from the end plugs) and was causing disk errors evident in the Windows event viewer, which actually were errors when chkdsk was used (you cannot always trust the event viewer drive errors as Windows presumes any drive is where you left it from your last Windows session, so if you move it, or it is new to the location on its USD bus, the event viewer will scream bloody murder until it learns the new location, where it will then proclaim the drive is healthy).
There appears to be a design deficiency in the hub: on both units I tested, there was too much noise on the final port #10 to plug in a cam. The cam image was very noisy and unusable. Plugging in the cam at the first port works around this design problem. Apparently, there is inadequate noise containment within the hub body, and this can cause slower transfer rates for hard drives and bad images for cams.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Doran", "review_title": "VIA Labs chipset - so far so good", "review_text": "So far so good. Will update review if anything changes - have audio interface and few devices plugged in, external hard drive, sd card reader - no issues.
For anyone curious about the chipset used, it's VIA Labs:
VIA Labs VID_2109 PID_0822 (USB 3.2 hub) Primary 3-port hub + 1 downstream port (USBC)
VIA Labs VID_2109 PID_0822 (USB 3.2 hub) Secondary 4-port hub off that downstream port (USBA)
VIA Labs VID_2109 PID_2822 (USB 2.1 companion hubs)
This was the only information I couldn't find before purchase, and was exactly what I was looking for - previously purchased a Amazon Basics 7 port usb3.1 hub and kept on getting errors in device manager. Seems like they just daisy chained a bunch of crappy hubs together to make it 7 port, and was bottle necked for throughput.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Antonio Aguilera", "review_title": "Es un hub súper versátil!", "review_text": "Uso mi Mac Mini M1 (que sólo tiene 2 puertos usb) principalmente para música. Tengo 7 teclados y/o controladores MIDI que ahora, gracias a este hub de 10 puertos, los puedo conectar todos simultáneamente y aún me sobran puertos para otros dispositivos usb, como memorias, discos duros, mi iPad, etc. Además, cada puerto tiene un switch on/off que funciona de dos maneras: si la Mac está apagada, le suministra corriente al dispositivo, haciendo funcionar a los dispositivos que son stand-alone. Si la Mac está encendida, además de suministrar la corriente, monta el dispositivo en la Mac. Esto me evita completamente estar conectando y desconectando cables usb. Lo recomiendo al 100%.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Antonio Cruz", "review_title": "Artículo que cumple lo que ofrece", "review_text": "Buen diseño y funcionalidad, recomendable", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Mikel Ballesteros", "review_title": "Recomendable 100%", "review_text": "Escribo una reseña real porque a mí me gusta leerlas.
Buena calidad de construcción, es pesado, metálico. Sin problemas conectando 8 discos duros externos auto-alimentados de 2.5'', y transfiriendo datos entre ellos.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Pedro", "review_title": "Excelente equipo", "review_text": "Solo conecte algunos dispositivos y todos funcionaron de maravilla", "review_rating": ""}]

Title: Belkin 100W 10Gbps Multiport USB-C Hub Adapter for Laptop, iPad, PC, & More
Description: 4-IN-1 USBC HUB: Connect multiple peripherals including camera/webcam, video capture cards, and more; Our 4-port Type C USB hub for laptop boasts 4 USB-C 3.2 Gen 2 ports for lightning-fast data transfer and upload speeds
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Keegan Q.", "review_title": "A hub is not a dock. This is a very good USB-C hub", "review_text": "Does what a hub ought to do - which is to say, you can plug it into one USB-C port and it will make power and data connectivity available to four downstream USB-C devices. The big caveats are that the host cable is extremely short and the power made available to downstream devices is significantly reduced from what the host provides. It's still a five star device because these short cables are universally present on all USB-C hubs, and the power limitations are less severe than other similar products that I have tested. Most importantly, the data connectivity offered by this unit is excellent, and it's extremely portable, being barely larger than the connectors it contains.
I would still very much prefer a version of this device with a USB-C female connector on the back instead of the permanently attached short cable but apparently there are valid technical reasons that USB-C hubs are not made in this way. Devices that offer more power and better cabling options are now classified as docks rather than hubs, they tend to be based on Thunderbolt rather than plain old USB-C, and some of these docks are quite excellent, but they are comparatively very expensive. This particular device is just a hub, it is very affordable compared to a dock, and it's as good as USB-C hubs get.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Father Goose", "review_title": "Belkin's USB-C Hub: A Reliable Winner!", "review_text": "Okay, so I'm pretty picky when it comes to my tech accessories, but Belkin almost always nails it. I've been a loyal customer for years, and their hubs and transfer wires are consistently top-notch.
This Belkin Connect 4 Port USB C Hub definitely keeps that streak going, it never lets me down. You get four USB-C 3.2 Gen 2 ports, each ready for ultra high-speed data transfers up to 10Gbps, which is fantastic for my external SSDs and other peripherals.
It's super handy for connecting all my gear, from cameras to a keyboard, and I've had zero issues with performance. The pass-through charging up to 100W is also a lifesaver, keeping my laptop juiced up while I use the hub.
Plus, the compact design and durable build mean I can toss it in my bag without a second thought. Belkin truly understands what users need in a reliable multi-port adapter.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Marty Babits, LCSW, BCD", "review_title": "Fine product", "review_text": "Good product something of a learning curve for a non technical user but in the end a solid product Do you know what an upstream port is? Do you now what a downstream port is. It's not hard to learn about it But I needed to consult ChatGPT To be able to use this hub effectively", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "William Herloski", "review_title": "Be aware of bad units being sold right now.", "review_text": "DO NOT BUY THIS!!
These USED to be a 5 star product from me, I've lost count how many I have purchased and included built into my products I manufacture. All of 2025 NO ISSUES at all, battle tested in the photo event industry buy some very large companies I have as clients. Come 2026 and the last two batch orders I have purchased I have had to replace 10 of them within a 2 month window, all for different customers because they stopped working in a short amount of time. Something happened in the Belkin manufacturing of these hubs in the past 3 months and I have lost my confidence in the stock that is available right now, I have moved to another HUB manufacturer for my products. I even tried calling Belkin quietly to make them aware of this issue and could not get anyone who cared that they had bad units being sold. So now it's to be very public about this issue and to let people know to be aware there ARE bad units in circulation of these hubs. ALWAYS have a backup on hand just in case! Sorry Belkin, you need to have a better process to receive feedback from other manufacturers that use your products in theirs. I hope I can regain confidence again someday.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Jenijen", "review_title": "Works in a Tesla", "review_text": "I own a 2020 Tesla 3 with a first generation cellphone charging system. This system will not charge the newer and larger cell phones like an iPhone 14 pro max with a case. Removing the case to charge the cellphone gets old. Tesla wants to charge an arm and a leg to update my current charging system, so I purchased this item. I disconnected the existing cellphone charging cord from my Tesla (Easy to do) and attached this multi port adapter from the car to a MagSafe wireless charger. Now my iPhone 14 pro max can be easily charged. Additionally, since this adapter has multiple ports, I was able to attach a second MagSafe wireless charging cord and simultaneously charge my husband’s iPhone 14 pro max (with case) while we are on long trips. The Tesla comes with a double charging system for 2 cellphones that sit next to each other and at a 45 degree angle. Attaching double sided tape to the back of the MagSafe onto the car’s charging system prevents the cord from sliding down. Very pleased and saved myself a ton of money", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "TriedAndTrue", "review_title": "Compact Hub With Fast Reliable Performance", "review_text": "I am giving this USB C hub 4 stars because it is a well designed accessory that makes it much easier to connect multiple USB C devices without taking up much space. The compact size fits easily into a laptop bag, making it convenient for travel, work, or keeping at a desk.
The four USB C ports are very useful for connecting accessories like external drives, webcams, audio devices, and other peripherals. File transfers have been fast and reliable, and I appreciate that each port supports high speed data transfer. The 100W pass through charging is another great feature because I can keep my laptop powered while still using the other ports without constantly swapping cables.
I also like that it works with a variety of devices, including laptops, tablets, and desktops that support USB C. The build quality feels solid, and everything connects securely without feeling loose.
The reason I am giving it 4 stars instead of 5 is that it is important to know this hub is focused on USB C connectivity only. If you also need USB A, HDMI, or SD card slots, you will likely need an additional adapter. Depending on your setup, that may limit its versatility.
Overall, this is a dependable and portable USB C hub that delivers fast performance and convenient charging. If your devices primarily use USB C, it is an excellent solution for expanding connectivity while keeping your workspace simple and organized.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "American Wireman", "review_title": "Need more USB-C ports AND passthrough power?", "review_text": "This hub is very handy if you need to use multiple USB-C peripherals but still need passthrough power for your laptop, 65 watts in my case. I have not experienced any noticeable difference in transfer speeds or heat. Typical Belkin high quality, all the ports are tight and connections feel secure.
I want to note that this unit will NOT allow HDMI functions via USB-C. I still need to plug my external display directly into the other USB-C port on my laptop.
The only downside is that the surface of the hub is a high gloss black, which will scuff like crazy the first time you toss it into your backpack or set it on the table. Does not at all effect functionality but can be annoying for some. Otherwise, this is now one of my essential daily tech accessories.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "NathanOr BenZvi", "review_title": "NathanOr BenZvi", "review_text": "High quality and super easy yo use", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "A Brief Elaboration of a Tube", "review_title": "Compatibility", "review_text": "I wanted this hub because I'm starting to experiment with videography on my iPhone 15 Pro, and the specs for data speed support and ability to support pass-through charging and other peripherals including a high-speed external drive made it seem ideal. And I'm sure it does all those things beautifully, but what it doesn't do is support charging of my iPhone..... which is a bit of a deal-breaker, really. Looking back, I see that the description doesn't actually mention support for iPhone 15 Pro, but iPad Pro and Mac compatibility (and support for supposedly universal USB-C devices) clearly doesn't include the iPhone. Very happy to accept that the reason for that is Apple and their outright stupid insistence on control of everything, but it doesn't really help me.....
I've often bought Belkin accessories and peripherals and it's a brand I trust, so my "Value for money" and "Charging power" scores relate only to my immediate experience and inability to charge my iPhone.
UPDATE 3 APR 2024:
I've left all my ignorant waffle above in place in case any other users find the difficulty I had - and judging by the numbers who can't get their iPad to charge, there are several of us. I did uprate my "star" rating as the problem isn't Belkin and not even Apple, for a change :-)", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Waveterm", "review_title": "Great !!", "review_text": "Perfect piece of utility gear", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "user-MKEBPT", "review_title": "جدا جميل وجبار", "review_text": "جدا جميل وجبار", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Pepe pecas", "review_title": "Chulada para iPhone XV Pro", "review_text": "Lo ocupo para grabar en ProRes con el iPhone y no tener que cargarlo con MagSafe además de conectar una tarjeta de sonido externa creative sound blaster para un micrófono sensheisser, estuve probando varios y ninguno soporto la tasa de transferencias ya que ProRes genera archivos descomunales", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Marc Hinderickx", "review_title": "Permet d'augmenter le nombre de ports USB-C de mon Mac M2", "review_text": "Fonctionne parfaitement. J'y connecte un disque en USB-C, un hub avec plusieurs disques en USB-2 et une connexion réseau en RJ45.
Toutefois, mon ecran BenQ qui aliment mon Mac en USC-C ne fonctionne pas au travers de ce concentrateur. Je dois le connecter directement sur le Mac; ce qui n'est pas un problème puisqu'il dispose de 2 ports USB-C.", "review_rating": ""}]

Title: UGREEN USB C Hub 4 Ports, Multiple USB 3.2 Hub, 4x10Gbps Data Transfer
Description: 4-Ports USB C Splitter: The 4-in-1 USB C hub transforms one of your laptop's USB-C ports into 4 USB-C data ports. Perfectly connect all your USB peripherals in your daily workflow to meet your present and future needs. (Note: The USB-C ports don't support video output or charging)
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "SiskiyouScoj", "review_title": "An effective low-cost expander", "review_text": "I have a relatively new Mac Mini M4, and I do find its ports somewhat limiting. The Mac has two USB-C in front and three Thunderbolt ports in the back. Because the Mac mini itself is so small and light, it can be difficult to access the ports and plug peripherals in and out. This UGreen USB hub works connected either to the USB ports in the front or to one of the Thunderbolt ports in the back. It doesn’t offer Thunderbolt speed, but it is quite quick and responsive for USB-C. I have had minor reliability problems with the ports on the M4—I have a USB keyboard, trackball, backup drive, and sometimes two external SSD drives plugged in, and the Mac itself sometimes doesn’t see everything at the same time—for instance, my trackball sometime disappears.
I’ve had this hub plugged into one of the USB-C ports in front and keep a number of peripherals plugged into it, and they have all worked very effectively at the same time, and the speed has been very responsive on the external data drives. So it has improved my Mac.
This is not heavy; it’s light plastic, but it works well. What I would have appreciated is if this had one USB-A port, too. I see a lot of USB-A hubs that have one C and a lot of As, but the new standard is USB-C. Some of my peripherals are USB-A, and I have little adapters that convert USB-A to USB-C and those work great with this, too, so with one of those, you can, of course, plug USB-A items into this.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Bruce G", "review_title": "Great Price and Quality. Nice to have additional USB C ports for external SSD's, YubiKeys, etc. Very lightweight and small form factor. Easily fits in my travel bag and requires no external power.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Jeremiah Hundley", "review_title": "Works well for me despite all the negative press", "review_text": "You know there’s a lot of bad comments here on this, but I’ve had one and had no problem. However, it will not power my MacBook Pro - at all! The power cord has to go directly into the computer.

Title: USB C Hub 7 Ports USB 3.0 Hub with 4*USB-A&3*USB-C (4ft)
Description: 【7 Ports USB 3.0 Hub】Xiaobi USB C Hub offers a versatile solution, expanding your device with 7 additional USB 3.0 ports. Perfect for connecting USB peripherals like flash drives, mice, keyboards, and printers.
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Vine Reviewer", "review_title": "Easy USB port expansion for my desk", "review_text": "I picked up this 7-port USB C hub because I had simply run out of USB ports on my docking station. Between my mouse, keyboard, speakers, webcam, and all the newer devices using USB-C, I needed an easy way to expand what I could connect without replacing my existing setup. The 4-foot cable is particularly useful on my desk because I can position the hub where it is convenient instead of having everything crowded around the back of the docking station.
I have been using it for the wireless dongles for my mouse and keyboard, along with my small Polycon speakers and webcam, and everything has worked perfectly for me. I like having four USB-A ports and three USB-C ports available in one place, especially as I am accumulating more USB-C devices. The aluminum housing feels sturdy, the non-slip base keeps it from sliding around, and the small LED lets me know it is powered. One thing to pay attention to is that the USB-C port marked 5V is for power input only, not data transfer, so it is not an additional data port. That is clearly stated in the description, but it is worth knowing before plugging something into it and wondering why it isn't recognized.
I think this is a practical solution for anyone who needs more USB ports without rearranging their entire computer setup. The long cable and combination of USB-A and USB-C ports make it especially useful on a desktop workstation. For my particular setup, it has done exactly what I needed and saved me from constantly swapping devices between limited ports.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Amazon Reviewer", "review_title": "Versatile and Well-Built USB Hub", "review_text": "Very pleased with this USB-C hub. Having seven ports in a compact enclosure is extremely convenient, especially when connecting multiple peripherals to a laptop or desktop with limited USB connectivity.
The four USB-A and three USB-C ports provide a useful mix for both older USB devices and newer USB-C peripherals. USB 3.0 speeds are also fast enough for transferring files to external storage and for everyday devices such as keyboards, mice, USB adapters, and other peripherals.
I particularly like the straightforward plug-and-play operation. There was no complicated setup or additional software required—just connect it to the computer and the ports are immediately available. The compact design also makes it easy to keep on a desk or take along with a laptop, its heavy weight keeps it from moving around when attached devices move around, a problem I've had with lighter-weight models.
Overall, this is a very practical USB expansion solution at a great price. The combination of seven ports, a good mix of USB-A and USB-C connectivity, compact size, and USB 3.0 performance makes it a useful addition to any computer setup. Highly recommended!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Crash", "review_title": "Nicely Designed USB Hub", "review_text": "The XIAOBI USB 3.0 7 Port Hub looks really nice. It is aluminum and has 7 ports, 3 USB C and 4 USB A all rated at 5Ggps. It does require a 3 Amp 5VDC power supply (not included -1 Star) of some sort if you are going to be using external hard drives and the like.
I am glad I got this hub because I had two other 10 port USB hubs connected I thought were connected to USB 3.0 ports but when I started speed testing this hub, I noticed they were only transferring at USB 2.0 speeds. I connected all hubs to legit USB 3.0 ports and the speeds increased by 5 times. Almost all the things I have connected to the USB hubs work fine at USB 2.0 speeds, dongles, wireless headset etc. but if you transfer files on to a thumb drive or an external hard drive; you want the USB 3.0 speed.
With the other two 10 port hubs connected; when I connected this hub to my system it started to do squirrely things. The Logitech mouse & keyboard didn’t work and thumb drives would not register on some hubs but would on other hubs. I think this is a problem of my system; too many USB ports connected so I removed this one.
I connected this hub to my windows 11 laptop as the only hub and it worked perfectly with no problems. So, if you have a power supply and only use this hub; you should be fine. I really do like the looks and speed of this USB hub.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Sbc", "review_title": "No more cord chaos in the living room entertainment center", "review_text": "I didn't realize how much I needed to clear up my messy living room hub center for cords until I plugged in this 7-port USB 3.0 hub from Xiaobi. The solid aluminum alloy build feels genuinely sturdy and doesn't slide around thanks to the non-slip rubber base, which also keeps my TV stand safe from annoying scratches. With seven ports available, I can easily leave the grandkids' Xbox, PS4, external media drives, and peripheral receivers plugged in all at once without constantly swapping cables. Transferring large video files and photos takes just seconds with the speedy 5Gbps data transfer, and the 4-foot cable gives me plenty of slack to route it neatly behind my entertainment center. It even comes with a handy dedicated 5V power input port on the back to keep all my devices running super stable under a heavy workload. At this price point, getting a slim, travel-friendly, and wide-compatible hub that works seamlessly across multiple systems is an absolute steal for the value.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Paul Archambault", "review_title": "Solid hub, passes USB 3.0 speeds with no loss.", "review_text": "For being a USB 3.0 rating, this is a good hub. Solid metal construction with a tapered angle front for easier access. Rubber strips on the bottom of the HUB keep it in place. It has a tight form factor, up to seven devices without over crowding while keeping the overall width to a minimum.
The input USB C port is on the rear of the chassis, along with an external power input (optional). For my desk design, the rear ports don't work out well, plugging the cables into the rear of the HUB chassis, pushed it out away from the rear wall of my desk. Side input ports work out better for me.
Throughput speed is what you would expect for a 3.0 USB rating, there is no discernable loss of speed using the hub, it seems to pass data without any loss of packets or bandwidth.
For a 3.0 hub, the price point makes it a good value.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Adam Mitskevich", "review_title": "Useful Mix of USB-A and USB-C Ports", "review_text": "I like the combination of ports on this hub. With four USB-A and three USB-C connections, it gives me more flexibility than hubs that heavily favor one connector type. The ports are spaced well and easy to access, and the metal housing has a solid feel.
The 4-foot cable is one of the more useful features for my setup. A lot of hubs have short cables that limit where they can be placed, while this one gives me enough length to position it where it is actually convenient on my desk.
It is also worth noting that this is primarily a USB data expansion hub. The additional USB-C connection on the back marked for power is there to provide supplemental power to the hub; it is not another data port or a charging port for connected devices.
Overall, this is a straightforward way to add several USB-A and USB-C connections while keeping everything organized in one compact hub.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "GoodErNah?", "review_title": "Nice Hub", "review_text": "This is a really cool design. I was actually surprised by how small and compact it is when it arrived, but in this case that’s definitely a good thing. It manages to pack a lot of utility into a very small footprint without taking up a bunch of unnecessary space.
The design makes really efficient use of the available room, and I like that you get quite a bit of functionality without having another bulky item sitting around. The speeds also seem nice and fast in my use, which makes it feel even more capable for something this compact.
Overall, I’m impressed with how much they managed to fit into such a small design. It’s clever, space-saving, fast, and practical. A lot of utility in a surprisingly small package.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Eye In The Sky", "review_title": "Excellent USB 3.0 5GBps Hub", "review_text": "This thing is great, it has 4 USB-A (3.0) ports and 3 UCB-C ports that support 5Gbps speed. This thing is solidly built, the frame is made of aluminum and it has a nice little desktop profile slant to it so it will look nice sitting on a desk top or as I will be doing, connecting it to sit on top of my Desktop Tower etc. I am going to be able to get rid of 2 cheap plastic hubs I had been using and boil everything down to this hub. Very nice quality, excellent value for money especially for those of you who, like me - have webcams, external harddrives, mouse, and other devices that connect via these interfaces. Very happy to modernize my IT layout here in my home office. Top marks from me.....", "review_rating": ""}]

Title: Logitech G413 SE Full-Size Mechanical Gaming Keyboard - Black
Description: Take your gaming skills to the next level: The Logitech G413 SE is a full-size keyboard with gaming-first features and the durability and performance necessary to compete
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "jeremy Gares", "review_title": "Light, bright, responsive, and with a wonderful profile layout", "review_text": "Best keyboard I've ever owned. Sturdy case, sleek profile, the layout makes this keyboard incredibly easy to clean without the need to dismantle the keys in the process. The White LEDs are bright and easy to see in the dark, unlike many backlit keyboards that can make it harder to read the keys. The responsiveness both in typing and in the tactile feel of every key clacking on release is a delight. I was skeptical when the sale brought the price below $35, but I could not be more impressed with the quality upon arrival. As a friend has been using a slightly different G4 model for 5 years, I have every expectation that I will be using this keyboard for years to come. Very happy customer.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Iain Ballas", "review_title": "Worth 60 bucks easy, on sale it's an absolute bargain.", "review_text": "I ordered one of these after my place of employment got tired of keyboards failing constantly. After several months of outright abusive use by my co-workers, they still performed flawlessly with a lovely sense of tactile feedback, soda spills aside. One failed only after half a thermos of coffee was spilled into it, but that's to be expected from anything not waterproof rated.
After ordering one for myself to use at home, I LOVE typing on it. It's my first true mechanical keyboard, and it's pleasant to just tap away, typing whatever I feel like. Each key feels like it's got two levels of depression (almost like me): First a clear 'catch' when the key activates and types, and then another more firm one when you reach the bottom of the key well. I've yet to have it double-type anything even when my clumsy fingers wanted to, although it hasn't saved me from butterfingering my keystrokes in games.
As far as gaming goes, it's not PERFECT. It does make an audible noise when typing, so when you are frantically spamming the strafe or jump keys, it's going to sound like clicking the mouse over and over, but it's really no worse than your average mouse. If you're wearing headphones and blasting your speakers, you won't notice it. If you're in a silent small room, you can't avoid hearing it. Find your medium.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Ian Long", "review_title": "Great Mechanical Keyboard for gaming or surfing the web.", "review_text": "Satisfying but quiet clicks, decent lighting, solid construction, and amazing responsiveness give this keyboard a 5 ⭐ from me. I game pretty much everyday and Logitech is the only keyboard/mouse company I find worthwhile AND affordable. As a major plus, it's also very ergonomic and easy to use for long periods of time.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "MarlinspikeCharlie", "review_title": "Perfect for me. I figured out the reason: painted letters and numbers wear off after a while. This see-through letters/numbers (presumably) will always remain. You don't use the keys unless plugged in anyhoo! So, I see no problem!
It's very nicely weighted and has a nice feel on the keys. Great for the $35 price I paid!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "MisterCroft", "review_title": "A solid offering", "review_text": "I like it. Well lit for a dark room, responsive, a little loud in a quiet room but not too bad, lack of a volume control knocks off a star. That should be standard on a gaming keyboard. Not bad.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "SJP", "review_title": "Excellent Keyboard for Everyday Work", "review_text": "I've been very happy with this keyboard for everyday work use. The mechanical keys have a great feel and make typing much more enjoyable, especially during long periods of writing and data entry. The build quality feels solid, and the keyboard has a clean, professional look that fits well in an office setup.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "RBK", "review_title": "Great keyboard with backlight with mechanical keys.", "review_text": "This is a mechanical keyboard. That means it is noisy where it has the traditional keyboard sound. I personally love it! The key are far more responsive than the soft-touch keyboards that are mostly used today. The clicking of the keys could be distracting to someone sharing an office, however, if you work in a private office, this keyboard is great. Also, the keyboard is backlit which makes it that much more useful when working late nights in a darker environment. It is constructed of metal and has a slip resistant base that stays put on my keyboard slide.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "brichards", "review_title": "Great Keyboard", "review_text": "I bought this keyboard after returning another one from a major retailer that the letters were wearing off of the keys after less than a weeks worth of use. I love how it lights up making the keys easy to see. This lighting feature can also be turned off for dimmed. It looks a little different from standard keyboards and it seems like the keys are just slightly closer together than a standard keyboard. I also like that it is not as wide as a standard Microsoft keyboard saving me a couple of inches on my desktop.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "user-MF84U8", "review_title": "Amazing", "review_text": "Very good", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Iskaral Pust", "review_title": "Great keyboard", "review_text": "I am using this keyboard right now to type this review. I got one of these for work, and I like it so much I bought another one for home. The brown switches have tactile feedback, but no audible click. The feel and sound of these keys while typing is very satisfying. This keyboard is a bit noisy, but I haven't heard any complaints about that so far. I much prefer this mechanical keyboard to my old membrane keyboards. I am still getting used to it, so I make a few typos, but the frequency of them is diminishing.
