Well, I would say it is excellent, one can usually rely on Logitech to provide a good product and this is a prime example.
The noise level is not the loudest I have heard from mechanical keyboards. Besides, if you want the responsiveness of a mechanical keyboard, you have to expect and accept a certain level of click-clack.
I use it mostly to play games and secondly to write stories, as such it works well. While I do not play professionally, or online, nor care to, during my usage I have not noticed any lag or ghosting.
In particular, I like the while lighting, it is not strong, but not weak either, allowing me to see the keys in any lighting situation. Which I appreciate, as the popular RGB keyboards are a bit too "loud" for me.
It is also very tight and small for a mechanical, and fits comfortably on a small desk.
I highly recommend this keyboard!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Jess Gonzalez", "review_title": "Fue un regalo", "review_text": "A la persona que se lo regale le encanta la marca logitech y se puso muy feliz asi que creo que esta muy bien", "review_rating": ""}]

Title: Razer Huntsman V3 HE Magnetic TKL 8KHz Wired Gaming Keyboard
Description: PRECISION FOR COMPETITIVE GAMING – Dominate FPS games and esports tournaments with Razer Hall Effect Magnetic Switches featuring Rapid Trigger and adjustable 0.1-4.0 mm actuation for faster reactions, cleaner movement inputs, and personalized control
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Pablo Ladino", "review_title": "A huge upgrade from my BlackWidow V3", "review_text": "I honestly didn’t expect to like this keyboard this much. I upgraded from a Razer BlackWidow V3, and the difference is immediately noticeable.
The magnetic switches feel incredibly smooth and responsive, and being able to adjust the actuation point and use Rapid Trigger is a game changer for competitive gaming. Movement feels much more precise, especially in Fortnite. The keyboard also feels extremely well built and premium.
What I really like is that it isn’t only great for gaming. For everyday use, studying, and programming, I can switch to a normal profile and it feels just as good to type on.
I was a little skeptical at first because I was already happy with my BlackWidow V3, but after using this one, I don’t think I could go back to a traditional mechanical keyboard.
If you’re coming from a regular mechanical keyboard, this is a serious upgrade. Absolutely love it so far. 🔥", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "HikerBrian", "review_title": "Incredible for coding, even better for gaming,", "review_text": "This one gets reviewed from two angles. As a professional software engineer I live by the quality of my keyboard and have been opinionated about keyboards for more than 20 years, so I ran this as my daily driver for a week to test it out. It was quiet, consistent, and responsive. Despite the gaming branding, this is probably the best tenkeyless keyboard I've ever typed on. Turn the lighting off and it can be dropped onto any office desk without getting a second glance. The high quality PBT keycaps have a texture that doesn't go slick and greasy, and they shouldn't shine up the way ABS does after a few months of heavy use. The switches are factory lubed with a dense foam layer underneath, so there's no hollow plastic rattle and no metallic ping. It's also not the clicking like you get from mechanical switches. It's a low, dull sound that doesn't get annoying in a quiet room or on a call. The adjustable actuation mattered more than I expected for office use. Setting it deeper than a gamer would means you stop firing off accidental characters when your fingers graze the home row, which is something that makes most fast-actuation boards frustrating for long-form writing and code. The aluminum top gives it a solid build, so it doesn't flex or walk across the desk, and the detachable USB-C cable means a longer lifespan.
After my week ended I handed it to my teenage son, the gamer, and I really don't think I'm getting it back. He found things I never would have. Rapid Trigger resets the key the instant it starts to rise instead of waiting for a fixed point, which he says completely changes counter-strafing. Snap Tap prioritizes whichever direction key you pressed most recently, so pressing A while holding D doesn't leave you standing there. Dynamic Keystroke lets a single key fire up to four different actions depending on how far down you press it, and Snap Flex assigns one action on press and a different one on release. He set up a key that peeks a corner on a light press and pulls back on release. I didn't even know keyboards did that, but he's raving about it. The 8000Hz polling means it reports to the PC eight times more often than a standard board. He swears he can feel it. I'm skeptical it's perceptible, but he's the one winning matches. All of the tuning lives in the browser based software, which allows you to adjust lighting, actuation and keybinds without installing anything.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "NhutDuong", "review_title": "Good", "review_text": "Good", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "AmazonReviewer", "review_title": "Love the design and layout, and the HE switches feels great! I also love the keycaps texture!", "review_text": "I have multiple razer keyboards from down to the 2010 black widow which is still going strong, and a few newer ones from last year and I love them, but when I saw this new huntsman V3 HE 65% keyboard I wanted to see how it was.
Build quality is very solid, it has a nice looking aluminum plate which is very sturdy and does not bend when I push hard on it, and it has a decent amount of weight to it which is not too light or too heavy. I also like that it has dual stage feet which most 65% keyboards do without with them, and I like the way they made the USB port going in the case so the cable can sit flush in it, which does help prevent wearing out the USB Type C port or getting broken.
And it feels really good while gaming or typing on it with the new HE magnetic switches, they are really smooth and has a nice clacky sound profile and it is very responsive, the PBT keycaps feels really good and I really do love the grippy texture they have on them that my fingers do not slide off them when gaming for long sessions, and they are shine through legends and they are very easy to see in the dark.
The rgb lighting looks really good which I have to say Razer always had the best RGB lighting in my opinion, which there is tons of effects to choose from and to make with the Synapse software, only thing I do notice is the backlighting is not really bright because they did choose to use a diffuser on the switches were the LED are at and the switches have a frosted housing to them, but I really not picky about backlighting on keyboards so it's not an issue for me, but it still looks really good. And you do have to use the software to change the lighting because it can't be done on the keyboard itself, only the brightness can be done on the keyboard itself, but a workaround with that is using the onboard memory which has up to 6 profiles which that can be used for different lighting effects and it works good that way.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "MK", "review_title": "Razer’s Hall Effect Switches Are a Major Improvement", "review_text": "Razer has made adjustable-actuation keyboards before, but its previous analog Huntsman models relied on optical switches. This is its first real move into the Hall effect keyboard space, and the switch change is not just a spec-sheet distinction. These new magnetic switches feel noticeably smoother and less scratchy than the optical analog switches I have used in the past, especially when pressing a key slowly or typing for longer periods.
They also retain a full 4.0mm range of travel, which is less common than I expected among Hall effect gaming keyboards. I can set a very shallow actuation point for movement keys in competitive games without making the entire board feel like a hair trigger. For typing, I prefer a deeper actuation and the full key travel because it feels more natural and gives me fewer accidental inputs. That flexibility makes the Huntsman V3 HE easier to live with as an everyday keyboard rather than something designed exclusively for ranked matches.
Rapid trigger works as expected, resetting each key based on movement rather than waiting for it to return to a fixed reset point. In shooters, directional inputs feel crisp and immediate, particularly when rapidly stopping, strafing, or changing direction. Snap Tap can prioritize the newest input between two movement keys, while Snap Flex adds another way to activate commands based on releasing a key. These features will matter most to serious FPS players, but the adjustable actuation is useful even outside competitive gaming.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Adam Darling", "review_title": "Elite Magnetic TKL Keyboard With Precision Control", "review_text": "The Razer Huntsman V3 HE Magnetic Tenkeyless is engineered as a competitive‑grade keyboard built around Hall Effect Magnetic Switches, offering adjustable actuation from 0.1 mm to 4.0 mm and a 100‑million keystroke lifespan (). This switch architecture eliminates debounce delay entirely, enabling instantaneous actuation and reset behavior that mechanical switches simply cannot match. The magnetic sensing provides exceptionally consistent input recognition, and the keyboard’s internal calibration system compensates for magnetic interference to maintain stable performance over time. Combined with the TKL layout, which frees up desk space for low‑sensitivity mouse movement, the Huntsman V3 HE is clearly designed for players who rely on precision micro‑adjustments and rapid directional changes.
One of the most defining features is Rapid Trigger, which allows keys to reset the moment they begin to rise rather than waiting for a fixed reset point. This dramatically increases responsiveness in FPS titles, enabling faster counter‑strafes, smoother movement corrections, and more reliable repeated inputs. Esports.gg’s testing highlights how Rapid Trigger transforms WASD control, making movement feel “snappy, predictable, and extremely responsive” — a sentiment that aligns with real‑world gameplay impressions. The keyboard also supports Dynamic Keystroke, allowing up to four actions on a single key at different actuation depths, and Snap Flex, which assigns one action on press and another on release. These features give competitive players granular control over movement, utility activation, and complex keybind setups, especially in games like Valorant, CS2, and Apex Legends ().", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Amazon Customer", "review_title": "Hall Effect Makes The Difference", "review_text": "Huntsman V3 HE Magnetic TKL 8KHz Wired Gaming Keyboard | Hall Effect Magnetic Switches, 8000 Hz Polling, Razer Snap Flex,Razer Snap Tap, Rapid Trigger, Adjustable Actuation
So this listing is for the v3 ten key less Hunstman v3 8K HE keyboard specifically designed for gaming with hall effect switches and snap tap actions. The keyboard has an 8000 Hz polling rate and has onboard memory to store profiles.
I have both the v1 and v2 version of this exact keyboard so comparing all three of these keyboards, they all have the exact same solid build quality and sound quality which is a quite thocky experience. The keyboards are solidly built and made of premium material which leads to a very comfortable typing experience. The keyboard is constructed of a solid plastic and metal material which makes them feel premium. The keyboard is about 14" x 5" x 2" high and weighs in with a heft and weight that allows it to sit solidly on your desk.
I have been using this keyboard exclusively for nearly two weeks now and it is now my daily driver. I am thoroughly impressed by the HE switches and how very comfortable it is to type on. The software is the one short area as the Synapse software really does not effectively work on Mac but it does sort of work on Windows but don't expect much. The keyboard itself is highly customizable and allows for full customization in color along with key press. Also there is no Linux support either but you can use SignalRGB to control lighting. Also Synapse itself really bogs down your PC and slowly causes a memory leak which means you need to regularly reboot your PC.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Terrorgod", "review_title": "Maybe im ready to give Razer another chance", "review_text": "The Razer Huntsman V3 HE Magnetic Mini keyboard is the latest addition to their Hall Effect Magnetic keyboard lineup. If you haven't been keeping up with keyboard technologies, compared to traditional keyboard switches made by companies like Cherry, they are now utilizing magnets and lasers to create a much more responsive key press reducing latency and allowing for customizable key actuation based on the users preference. I am a hobbyist with keyboard tech, where I have built a good variety of keyboards with DIY kits, customized some of my own, and tend to go out of my way to try new technologies. This is my third time trying a Hall Effect keyboard, with my first being the Steelseries Apex Pro ( with HyperMagnetic switches) and the original Razer Huntsman.
I didn't hold onto either of those keyboards very long as at the time they were very expensive compared to their traditional counterparts. They also didn't wow me out of the box with their switch technology. Keypresses felt weak, as if there was no feedback to register that I had hit a key. It also took a lot of tweaking to get them to what I would consider a usable state with accurate typing. Which leaves me with the new Razer Huntsman, where I am happy to report it doesn't share any of these problems.
The recent revisions have made many changes, improving the texture on the keycaps, the sound of the keypresses, the out of box actuation is exactly what I want, and the 8khz polling is probably helping with how responsive the keys feel. I generally use full size keyboards as I like to have a numpad, but the feel of this keyboard is winning me over to make it my daily driver away from my Mountain Everest Max with Cherry Blues. Lubed Holy Panda switches are the only ones I own that might feel a little bit better than these, but the overall responsiveness of these HE Magentics is something I haven't had the pleasure of experiencing before.", "review_rating": ""}]

Title: Logitech MX Mechanical Wireless Illuminated Keyboard Tactile - Graphite
Description: Tactile Quiet mechanical key switches with a satisfying tactile bump you feel - for precise feedback, reactive key reset, and less noise so your typing doesn't disturb those around you
Category: Electronics,Computers & Accessories,Computer Accessories & Peripherals,Keyboards, Mice & Accessories,Keyboards
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Yo_Paisan", "review_title": "Never thought I'd love a keyboard so much...", "review_text": "It's taking a little getting used to the slightly different arrangement of some keys but man... overall, this keyboard KICKS TAIL!!! I love how it lights up, I'm always working in low light or the dark and my eyes aren't what they used to be so I just can't tell you how much of a difference it makes. I also feel like the key symbols won't/can't wear out because they're backlit. Typical keyboards have letter and words wear off over time, but I don't see how that's possible with this keyboard. It's not a "gamer keyboard" it's just a great basic keyboard with all the functions you need. Keystrokes feel amazing! Not sure how to describe but when you're typing it just feels really nice. A real quality built product and worth every penny. I'm considering buying another before they don't make them anymore... LOL Oh, the battery lasts forever on this thing too. You can turn it OFF when you're done for the day and you can set the keyboard to pair/work with multiple computers (even have keys configured differently if you like). The backlight shuts off when you remove your hands from the keyboard or stop typing for about 5 seconds, but its got this really cool "motion detection" feature that once you put your hands over the keys again or start typing it lights right back up! I'm telling you if you're in the market for a new BLUETOOTH keyboard and are willing to pay a little more for a NICE one... this is the board to have!!! I really love it. I'll give you the 1 thing I didn't like about it as I began using it... The FUNCTION ROW of keys has no space above the NUMBERS or Number pad, etc. So it's super easy to hit the wrong keys sometimes. I'll often go to use the "home" key and end up hitting the key to switch between machines, or the biggest one is the "lock" key the farthest top right key over the number pad's "minus/dash" key. I often go to hit the "minus/dash" key and end up locking my windows (having to sign in again). HOWEVER, using the Logitech software that is used to configure the keyboard I was able to just disable that lock key. I don't need a KEY for that anyway. When I want to lock my Windows session (log out) without shutting down, I'll just do it the normal way with my mouse (Start > Power > Lock). No big, been doing that forever anyway. Anyway, this keyboard is awesome. Especially, once you get used to it. Most times I get a new keyboard and have to get used to the key arrangements and different spacing anyway. Might as well do it with a great keyboard. 😊👍🏻 P.S. I have always been a Microsoft keyboard/mouse kinda guy. I didn't think much of Logitech until I got the MX Master 2 Mouse, which is now also my favorite ever. This keyboard goes with that mouse it's sold in bundles they're of the same product set.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "VChu", "review_title": "Satisfying typing experience", "review_text": "I love this keyboard. I use the same monitor for my gaming PC and for my work Surface Pro. I had a wired keyboard which I had to unplug from the gaming PC and plug into the docking station every morning and then do the reverse after my work hours. It became tedious after a while, so I decided to upgrade to a wireless keyboard that can switch between multiple devices without having me crawl under my desk to do so.
This one seemed not too expensive, had full width, and reviews were decent. I'm very pleased. Switching between devices is handled with 3 dedicated buttons for this specific purpose, no crawling required. I used the dongle to pair it with the gaming PC, and Bluetooth to pair it with my work computer. Now I can work from the kitchen or the yard if I want to.
It's slightly louder than I expected, but is by no means clickety like some others I've used. Typing is now completely satisfying. The texture of the buttons is soft and the feedback is addictive and makes me want to type forever.
As an unexpected bonus, I was able to connect the keyboard to my phone and type in mobile apps with a full keyboard!! What a novel and refreshing experience.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "BigReg26", "review_title": "Great first mechanical keyboard", "review_text": "I just finished my first long work session with this keyboard. I'm glad I bought it. It's very easy to type on. It's my first mechanical keyboard of any kind. I went with the quieter version. You still get the clicking sounds, just not super loud. I finally understand what people mean when they say typing on a mechanical keyboard feels more satisfying compared to non-mechanical ones. Highly recommend this keyboard if you're looking to get into mechanical keyboards. Definitely won't be my last.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Loki", "review_title": "Beautiful keyboard", "review_text": "So I just received and began to use this keyboard today. I am pretty blown away by how nice it looks, how good it feels, and just the experience overall. Compared to my previous keyboard, I already like this a fair amount more. For reference, I was using the Corsair k57 RGB wireless. Also a quite nice keyboard, but this has a much more premium feel. It's also much more professional looking, which is why I chose it as I plan to use this in an office environment. Some thoughts below.
-The clicks are super nice, I've never used a "clicky" switch with feedback like this before and I quite enjoy it. Probably my favorite feedback I've had from just typing on a keyboard. The various corsair boards I've used in the past I typically chose a quiet and/or a linear switch.
-Overall a very nice, professional look. I wouldn't expect any weird looks with a keyboard like this in a professional environment.
-Pairing was easy, plugged in the receiver and it instantly connected; no other input needed. Even the sister product to this never did that for me, the MX master 3S mouse. I had a bit of a struggle trying to get that to pair using the included receiver, as I recall. (Otherwise one of my favorite mice, also coming from a mostly corsair brand background). There is also bluetooth pairing, if preferred. (or if the receiver refuses to work, like my MX master 3S.)", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Edward Buchmann", "review_title": "It's Logitech. Can't beat it.", "review_text": "If you need a keyboard that fits in a crowded desktop or you just like a clean and neat desk looks, and if you work with applications that require precision on what you type, coding, CAD, the feel and precision of a mechanical keyboard is what you need. Love it. I've heard it's great for games too, but I don't play games at all, so I can't tell, but I bet durability required for games is similar to software coding, tons of strokes per minute. Games are certainly more rough, due to adrenaline, that can be hard on a keyboard. Not my thing, I need precision, and compact format.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Alexander R Adams", "review_title": "Very disappointing for a $150+ keyboard.", "review_text": "I was very disappointed when I started using this overpriced keyboard.
First of all, the build quality is inexcusable for a $150+ keyboard, especially from a brand like Logitech. The space bar and the backspace keys squeak horribly every time I press them. I understand that can be fixed by applying some white silicone grease, but I shouldn't have to do that with an expensive keyboard right out of the box. In addition, the rubber foot across the back of the keyboard has already started to peel off.
I purchased the tactile (quiet typing) version, and while it isn't the loudest keyboard I have ever typed on, "quiet" is not at all how I would describe it. Someone in the next room or cubicle would definitely be able to hear you typing on this. I wonder how loud the "clicky" version is...
And now, to address the backlight issue: Several reviews have mentioned problems with the backlight. It seems to function "as intended", but the design choices really make me scratch my head. The backlight will turn off just a few seconds after you stop typing, and doesn't turn on again until you press a key. That means that if you aren't constantly typing, the backlight will be turning on and off in a way that is very visually distracting at the bottom of your vision. If you take your hands away from the keyboard, you will not have the keys illuminated to help orient your hands when you start typing again. In a dark room that means you can't see anything on the keys. Even the timing of the backlight is inconsistent. Sometimes it turns off while I am still typing, sometimes it stays on for a minute or two with no input, like it got stuck.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Valkyrie99", "review_title": "Worthy Upgrade", "review_text": "I replaced a Logitech 860 with the MX, the quality and feel of the MX is very good. I love the feel of the keys. The key setup is more tighter than the 860, but after a couple days I’ve became accustomed to it and I like it. The difference in the feel and quality is significantly better than the 860.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Daniel C.", "review_title": "Beware the USB dongles", "review_text": "Original review: It's a keyboard an it works
After hearing people rave about mechanical keyboards, I decided to get myself one. I am not sure how representative of mechanical keyboards this one is, but I find it to be very similar to everything I have used before. The keys don't feel "clicky" at all. In fact, I am constantly running into an issue of resting my hands on the keyboard, and "mushing down" a key by mistake (in other words, "wwwwwwwwwwwwwwwww" because my finger pressed a key without me even noticing).
I think I can get used to pulling my hands away from the keyboard to keep that from happening, but I find it weird that I now have to do this. I assumed the keys would be harder to press, not mushier than the cheap-o keyboards I have had.
Another issue I have had is that the keyboard is not flat. I have tested it on multiple surfaces, including a glass table. I ended having to prop one side up with some paper. Not too happy about that.
For whatever reason, this does not have a print screen key. Luckily you can remap it using the Logi Options+ software.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Phillip H", "review_title": "Lovely Product - but US layout not clear in product description", "review_text": "Product is excellent, but be aware this is a US layout keyboard. If you want a UK layout (or European) you need to look for this specifically on Amazon.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Guy", "review_title": "Best office keyboard to date", "review_text": "This keyboard is pretty amazing. I own a HHKB, and a Pok3r. I build and customize my own keyboards. I bought this mainly because of the Logitech Flow feature. But first, I wanted to talk about the keyboard itself and why I think this is the best office keyboard to date.
The build quality is amazing. It's sturdy, and the internals are very tight, which means, no rattling, no added noise or reverbiation. As a result, this is a very quiet mechanical keyboard (I can only speak for the brown switch version).
The keycaps are made out of recycled plastic, but they don't feel cheap. They are quite smooth and easy to type with. The typing experience is very consistent and smooth (see type test photo). My typing speed is consistent with my other keyboards, but for me, it's definitely feels much better to type with tactile silent switches compared to my other keyboards.
Even though this keyboard is a low profile keyboard, there are flip up feet at the bottom of the keyboard to lift it up a little more to get a better angle if that's what you prefer.
The lights are nice, but what makes this keyboard really stand out is when it doesn't use the lights at all. Without the backlights on, this keyboard can do 10 months on 1 charge, which is completely unheard of for a mechanical full size wireless keyboard. I've had this keyboard for a couple of days on the whole time, and by now, my other wireless 60% would have died and required a recharge.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Amazon Customer", "review_title": "An Excellent Successor to the Venerable K800 Wired/Wireless Keyboard - Different but AWESOME!!", "review_text": "I really like this keyboard!!!
In fact, I would say that this is a good/reasonable successor to the magical, venerable K800 Wireless and Wired
I (like most) have an old wired K800 (attached to my work laptop), and was sooooo sad to see that I couldn't get another one. I took the leap and purchased the K800 wireless as a backup (what I writing this on..) for my personal laptop, and it truly is such a wonderful easy feeling keyboard.
Again, logitech has discontinued the wireless one - enter to MX Keys (full size)
I think that this one has that old school IBM-style feel, yet waay more robust, heavy (surprisingly), and modular (regarding key caps and triggers)
I think, if past is prologue (as it invulnerably i..) this product to will either disappear, or get worse - I will by a 1 or 2 for safe keeping", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Philip Jones", "review_title": "Does not state that this is a US keyboard layout (on sale in the UK)", "review_text": "This is a US layout keyboard on sale in the UK... but no mention of that on the description.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "A. Simpson", "review_title": "Excellent keyboard with a few minor issues", "review_text": "This keyboard is a solid little keyboard. It’s very well built and has a satisfying feel and noise while typing. I really like how easy it is to switch between different computers. I have it set to use both my desktop PC and my MacBook Air when I dock it on my desk. It knows which is which and changes the keyboard layout accordingly. Everything just works. The battery life is excellent and it charges up really quickly over usb c. The Logitech Options app is really easy to use with everything laid out in such a way to just make sense. Also; the back lighting is simple but still nice.
Ok onto my complaints. First I wish the key caps were a better material. They get glossy really quick from the slightly dirtiest fingers. I dunno if that’s due to the dark grey colour or the material itself. But for the price it should have better key caps. Second; I wish this thing had full rgb backlighting. The white is nice; but full colour would be better. Ok that’s it.
So overall this is a great desktop keyboard that you could also take with you if you wanted to use your laptop or iPad on the go with it. It’s great for multi device use and the typing experience is really nice!! If you’re coming from the keyboard that came with your Mac or PC… or want something small and portable; this is definitely for you!", "review_rating": ""}]

Title: AULA F75 75% Wireless Mechanical Keyboard, Hot Swappable Creamy Keyboard, Pre-lubed Linear Switches, 2.4GHz/Type-C/BT5.0, RGB Backlit Gaming Keyboards(White&Brown)

Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "aya holland", "review_title": "LOVE my first mechanical keyboard", "review_text": "This is the first mechanical keyboard that i got and i absolutely love it. It definitely makes the typing experience more relaxing - the keys have the perfect creamy think to it. If you type really fast it sounds like pebbles in the creek ^.^
I did some research before getting a keyboard since i wanted something of a good quality but was prepared to drop $100+ on it. Very pleased with the quality of t his one - it feels very sturdy, the keys have just enough resistance to effortless typing.
With the knob you can switch different color modes and adjust the brightness or control volume.
It also allows pairing with 3 devices (and switch with a brass of a button, well, 2 buttons but u get it) via Bluetooth and it’s very convenient since i can use it with my computer, iPad and steam deck.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Aub", "review_title": "Smooth and Satisfying Mechanical Keyboard", "review_text": "This keyboard has a great feel right out of the box. The pre-lubed switches provide a smooth, satisfying keypress, and the sound is pleasant without being excessively loud.
The 75% layout is a great balance between compact size and functionality. It keeps the important navigation and arrow keys while taking up considerably less desk space than a full-size keyboard. The wireless connectivity is also convenient and makes for a cleaner setup.
The hot-swappable design is a major plus for anyone who enjoys customizing their keyboard. Being able to change switches without soldering gives you plenty of options to personalize the typing experience later.
The keys feel responsive and consistent, whether I'm typing or gaming. The overall construction also feels solid, especially for the price.
Overall, this is an excellent mechanical keyboard with a smooth typing experience, useful wireless functionality, and plenty of customization potential.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Lauren Jeane", "review_title": "Amazingly creamy clicky clacks on a budget!", "review_text": "For a stock budget keyboard, I am *in love*. The sound is gorgeous; deep and thocky and super creamy. Sounds like rain on a tarp in the best way. It is super comfortable to use and the keys take very little pressure to press, so typing on this is a breeze. It feels sturdy and heavy and substantial, not cheap, light and rattly. This definitely feels like a quality keyboard and I highly, highly recommend it to those who are particular on their keyboard sounds!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Lauren Porcaro", "review_title": "Good for work", "review_text": "Creamy, adorable, lights are amazing, perfect size, lovely blue! It’s just an amazing product. It comes with a key switcher thing and extra keys in case. It also has a usb so you don’t have to plug it in and it is amazing with computer and has no glitchy features.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Nicholas", "review_title": "Keyboar", "review_text": "I mean you can't complain with the price. Overall, a good keyboard with decent features.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "mili", "review_title": "So pretty, amazing sound, easy connection⭐️", "review_text": "Obsessed! The pink and cream color combination is gorgeous in person. It’s so clean and cute and the RGB makes it even prettier. It comes with the strawberry mint switches and the keys feel so good to type on (buttery?) and the sound is so satisfying and thocky. I also love how easy it is to switch between devices. It feels really sturdy and it’s honestly one of my favorite desk purchases! 5/5 ⭐️", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Kay", "review_title": "Amazing keyboard, sturdy, lovely sound", "review_text": "i am very picky about my keyboards but this is the second AULA keyboard i have gotten and i am in love once again. the videos and pictures don’t do it justice it looks and sounds amazing, i love creamy / thocky sounding keyboards and this one is perfect.
the resistance on the keys is great, the sound is great, the whole thing is great so i definitely recommend getting this if you’re thinking about it, it is worth the money 100% it is so nice to type on and i use the usb connector ( my cats are going through a wire chewing stage) and its great.
i also love the adjustability of the keyboard, i always have the back end sit up higher, the material is solid and it feels super weighted which i love. there are a bunch of different color options i didnt show all of them in the video but i normally have mine on white or off.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "alfie", "review_title": "AULA F75 Review Glacial Blue Reaper Switches", "review_text": "I’ve been using the AULA F75 keyboard as my main keyboard, and it has been a great upgrade from my previous one, especially considering the price. I mainly use it wired, but I also tested the Bluetooth connection and it worked perfectly fine with no issues. The overall connectivity has been excellent, and I haven’t had any problems using it with my games.
The RGB lighting looks really nice and adds a lot to the keyboard’s overall appearance. I do wish there were more RGB customization options and selections available, but the included effects are still enjoyable and look great.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Jin", "review_title": "The best sounding keyboard!", "review_text": "I’ve used the AULA F75 for over six months, and it delivers outstanding typing and gaming performance. The 75% layout saves space without sacrificing functionality, and the volume knob is a practical addition. Tri-mode connectivity (wired, 2.4GHz, Bluetooth) is reliable, with no lag in gaming. Battery life lasts over a week with RGB off.
Build quality is solid, with durable PBT keycaps and minimal wobble. My only note: the **backlight isn’t shine-through**, so RGB is subtle unless keycaps are upgraded.
For its price, the AULA F75 offers premium feel, sound, and versatility. Highly recommended.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Jay", "review_title": "No APP, But Great Keyboard", "review_text": "Unfforunetly this keyboard doesn't have an app for mac, Have to use other software to for tweking stuff on the keyboard( whihc is a pain). Quality is 5/5.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Manini Nair", "review_title": "Must recommend", "review_text": "Genuinely beautiful keyboard I’m in love with it, there are multiple options with lighting and it’s a great value for money.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Juliana", "review_title": "LINDO!!!", "review_text": "Chegou uma semana antes do previsto <3 O teclado é muito lindo, tô apaixonada. Enfim, pra ser um teclado top de linha só faltou a construção em alumínio, mas pelo preço vale muito, ainda mais se estiver em promoção. 10/10", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Harshan Kumar", "review_title": "If you are willing to spend for it, just dont give it a second thought. This is a BLIND BUY !", "review_text": "The AULA F75 White is an absolute stunner. Title: AULA F99 Wireless Mechanical Keyboard,Tri-Mode BT5.0/2.4GHz/USB-C Hot Swappable Custom Keyboard,Pre-lubed Linear Switches,RGB Backlit Computer Gaming Keyboards for PC/Tablet/PS/Xbox
Description: Multi-Device Connection: The F99 wireless mechanical keyboard provides three connection methods, including BT5.0, 2.4GHz wireless mode, and USB wired mode. It can be connected to up to five devices at the same time, and switch between them easily by FN and key combination keys. No limits about your keyboard connection to meet the needs of work, gaming, and study
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Jackson", "review_title": "Love it!", "review_text": "Bought this for my wife’s WFH setup. She fell in love with the Creamy Switch craze on TikTok and this was a reasonably priced keyboard that fit the bill. I found a cute sakura themed keycap set to replace these, but she said she’d have been happy with the blues and purples that came preinstalled.
It looks great, feels and sounds fantastic, and does everything you’d want from a keyboard. She loves the size, specifically that it includes the number pad. Connecting is super easy. We’re using the hardwired USB-C option, but I was able to use Bluetooth on my laptop at work while I was testing and installing the other keycaps prior to giving this as a birthday gift. She loves that it’s such a lightweight feel of typing, even noticeably so to someone without the heavy handed typing of myself, having grown up on IBM and Alps switches which allow for some decent banging.
I’m not a keyboard snob or really a deep enthusiast, but some of my friends and coworkers that care more than I do really loved it as well. It’s a crowd pleaser, and that wonderful little subdued THOK on each tap is soothing as foretold.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "galactic-tide", "review_title": "Perfect for work and the sound is ohh so goood!!!", "review_text": "I LOVE this keyboard!! After spending two weeks researching I decided on the Aula F99 and I am so happy with my decision. I’m not a gamer but wanted a full keyboard for work and this checked all the boxes. The sound is so creamy and reminds me of marbles or smooth stones. It’s so fun to type on and the RGB is kinda fun too. Bluetooth connected with ease, so did wired. Haven’t tried the dongle yet but so far it’s been plug and play play with no issues. Feels sturdy not cheap. Sounds great out of the box. Ordered the Gatreon Milky Yellow switches but I may not even need them cuz I’m kinda digging this sound already. It’s soooo satisfying. Great value!!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Sora", "review_title": "First mechanical keyboard ever - love it!", "review_text": "Perfect right out of the box. Set up was effortless. I love the simple and minimalist look and layout of it. I decided to swap my old HP wireless keyboard that I use for work out for this one and while it's a tad bit louder than I expected for snall office settings, I still love the sound and feel of it. It is definitely "stockier" than expected for plastic. Bit on the heavyside in comparison to a standard HP keyboard. Feels good and solid though. I've been using it all day and have no complaints so far.
Small side note: if you're a dingus like me, the ÷ key on the number pad is the same as /. Took me a minute to figure that out because I'm so used to / + - * 🤣", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Lee", "review_title": "Bought it for my husband and now it's mine", "review_text": "First I want to say that I initially bought this for my husband as he had bought a walmart clicky brand keyboard and was finally growing tired of the clicky sound lol. Well as the keyboard enthusiast I suggested this one as it was simple and a few of the review videos had sounded promising.
When it arrived the first thing I noticed was the heft, this was made with durable material and not light weight at all, which put some ease to my mind that it wasn't just made of cheap plastic. The size was just perfect, I couldn't be happier, and when I typed for the first time the creamy and thocky sound just itched the right place in my brain. I could not get enough of it.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Maddie", "review_title": "Decent keyboard", "review_text": "Coming up on almost a year of owning this keyboard. It was just what I needed. I love the feel of the keys, the sound, the 3 different options to connect, the weight and the number pad. The battery life wireless is okay. I wish there was a power button. Sometimes you accidentally touch a key after turning off the computer and the keyboard feels like it stays on forever lol. I use it for my WFH job and light gaming. I bought it last April and now it’s February and I’m starting to notice connection issues (non responsive) and sticky keys. It’s been acting a bit possessed lately. I work with a lot of VDIs so that could also play apart in the weirdness but it’s been more and more frequent lately. I use the Bluetooth option, I will try to hardwire to see if there is a difference. Will update my review if it poops out 🤔🤔", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Corinne", "review_title": "Amazing Keyboard for WFH", "review_text": "I’ve had this keyboard for almost 2 months now and wanted to wait to write a review until I had used it for a while. I’ve got to say this keyboard is awesome. recently got a WFH after only ever working in an office so I knew I wanted to invest in a nice keyboard. I spent at least a week researching and reading reviews on keyboards and didn’t realize how hard it would be to find nice keyboard with a num pad but I kept coming back to this one because of the amazing reviews and of course I love the way it sounds! For the average person yes this is a little bit on the pricier side but to me it was totally worth it, I like that it has 3 forms of connection (Wired, Bluetooth, and USB), there are a million different RGB options and it sounds amazing and it comes with super easy instructions and you can change the key caps if you want nicer keys. I will say, as you can see in the video I have two keys where the lighting under them doesn’t work/ change color, but I still have it 5 stars because it doesn’t affect the function of the key board. Another slight inconvenience is that you do have to charge it with the wire after a few days if you’re using Bluetooth or USB and it doesn’t give a low power warning but besides that it’s perfect. I also want to note that I have seen that this key board had gone a little viral on TikTok and I did purchase before it was trending so I would say if you are coming here from TikTok no, it’s not a scam it’s actually a great keyboard!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "julia", "review_title": "Great keyboard for the price", "review_text": "The Aula F99 is a "96%" mechanical keyboard that comes in around the $90 price point normally, but can get as low as $60 on sale. That form factor means that it does have a numpad and arrow keys as well as home, delete and page up/down keys, but those keys are moved up in-line with the function keys and the numpad/arrow keys are squished up closer to the main keys with the arrow keys set a little further down to make space. Having a numpad was a must for me because I like to play games that often use the numpad for important functions, and I also prefer typing numbers on a numpad when the occasion arises. At this price point, this is probably one of the best options for people who want a numpad and/or arrow keys but still want a keyboard that looks and sounds more like a custom keyboard you see in YouTube shorts of people doing sound tests.
It has linear switches meaning there's no "bump" or clickiness to them, I'm not 100% sure what exact switches they are because there is some conflicting information online. I think mine has "Star Vector" switches? Regardless, the switches are quite light on force and very quiet, which brings us to the sound. This keyboard sounds great for the price. It's a little on the clacky side, but the switches have no scratchiness to them and are obviously pre-lubed, and there appears to be some kind of sound-deadening material inside the case as there is none of that hollow pinginess you get from something like a cheap Logitech mechanical. Overall it is a massive improvement from the Logitech keyboard I had previously to this one.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "AC2MO", "review_title": "My favorite keyboard to date!", "review_text": "I've had a few mechanical keyboards before, but this one so far is my favorite. The creamy switches have an amazingly satisfying feel and sound. Enough tactile feedback to know you hit the key, a bit "thocky", but not so clacky as to be annoying or overly loud. The condensed layout takes a bit of getting used to, but that's true of any "less than 100%" sized keyboard. The only key that bothers me a bit in the layout is the "0" on the numpad, but I'm getting used to it. I haven't played with the lighting much, but it definitely helps visibility in low light. Bluetooth connection has been rock solid, and the battery life even with the lighting on has been phenomenal; after a few weeks of moderate use, I have yet to have to charge it. Overall I'm extremely happy with the purchase, highly recommend it... it's definitely a leader in "bang for buck" vs some of the higher priced brands!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Jose lara", "review_title": "Ojalá siga así por mucho tiempo. 😄", "review_text": "Excelente teclado por su precio. Tiene muy buena calidad de construcción, las teclas se sienten cómodas y agradables al escribir y jugar, y la batería me ha dado un buen rendimiento. Además, la iluminación y el diseño le dan una apariencia muy premium. Hasta ahora ha superado mis expectativas y ha sido una de mis mejores compras. Tive teclados como razor blackwidow e ele é superior.
E o melhor, vem padrão abnt2!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Shivam Verma", "review_title": "BEST KEYBOARD!", "review_text": "The best in class Keyboard I have ever used! The Typing Experience just feels awesome! Earlier, I was using Dell Wireless!
Saw some Video on Social Media, and Man'O'Man! FELL IN LOVE WITH THIS KEYBOARD!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Jazz", "review_title": "Best Keyboard in My Collection!", "review_text": "I have had this keyboard for a month now, and wow! It is by far the best keyboard in my collection. I love a nice creamy typing experience, and this more than delivers. I had been searching for a full keyboard that was versatile and easy to use. Title: Kisnt KN85 Wireless Mechanical Keyboard, 75% Layout, Bluetooth/2.4GHz/USB-C, Custom RGB Backlit, Hot-Swappable Linear Switch, Creamy Sound for Gaming/Typing (Retro Beige)
Description: 【75% Space‑saving Layout】The KN85 series is a compact 85‑key keyboard (13.68" × 5.51" × 1.77") that keeps all the essentials (F1–F12, arrows, shortcuts) without the number pad. It frees up 25% of desk space for better mouse movement. Designed for small desks, laptop setups, gamers and minimalists. For frequent number‑pad input, choose our full‑size KN104 with a complete dedicated numpad, or opt for our new KN98 model — compact 99‑key that retains the numpad while saving desktop real‑estate
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Jen Degenhardt", "review_title": "Genuinely the best budget keyboard out there", "review_text": "I can’t recommend the kisnt KN85 enough. The RGB is bright (although the software isn’t great), It’s a good weight for a plastic keyboard, the colors it comes in are attractive, and the price is amazing. The most important part (to me) is the switches. They are Bsun purple switches, a smooth, creamy linear switch that sounds amazing. I genuinely use these in my other boards. It is made of plastic, but the plastic is sturdy. It is bluetooth, 2.4 ghz, and wired. Overall, this keyboard is worth it. I love this keyboard, i’ve bought two of them!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Harrison Phillips", "review_title": "Best board for the price, BY FAR !!", "review_text": "Great board especially at this price point. This really raises the bar for entry level products and makes it much more accessible. This thing will impress most seasoned enthusiast. I could see this thing attaining a similar status to the Aula F75.
You get really good acoustics, great switches (lubed BSUN Purples), gasket mounting AND hotswap.
I've been typing on it for a few days and the sound tests you see online are very accurate, board sounds very creamy and poppy, which makes for a very satisfying typing experience.
The RGB on this board is really bright and has some cool preset animations.
Definitely NOT office friendly, I took this thing to the office one day and had to swap it for a normal keyboard because it is quite loud. I enjoy the sound but I don't think my coworkers did. lol
Unfortunately I did notice that the space bar seems to make a really loud thunk which doesn't match the sound of the rest of the board, but you can fix this pretty easily with a rubber O-Ring or some foam inside the space bar.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Keith S", "review_title": "Super impressive for the price.", "review_text": "I'm shocked at the quality of this keyboard for the price. The main case is plastic but a is very good quality plastic. Obviously, it's not going to be aluminum at this price. The quality of the keycaps is also excellent. They are the more premium PBT plastic rather than the cheaper ABS plastic and they feel great. It even has more features than my other higher end mechanical keyboard as this one not only has wired USB (obviously), but also 2.4 Ghz dongle (which secures nicely in a little cutout of the bottom of the keyboard and held in magnetically), and a whooping 3 Bluetooth channels so you can pair this keyboard with many different devices at the same time.
I love the layout as well. It's a little smaller than a TKL layout keyboard, but without any compromises. Typically, I don't like 75% or less because you lose too many useful keys or they have them in a weird place, but this keyboard's layout is perfectly done. You still have all of your Home, End, PgUp, PgDn, Insert, Delete, and Print Screen and Pause/Break keys. The only key missing is the Scroll Lock key which is never used anyway so this is perfect.
It has nice RGB that lights up under and around the keys. Also comes with some extra switches and even a decent keycap and switch puller tool. Even comes a thin, cheap, plastic dust cover which I appreciate.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Michael", "review_title": "It's pretty good!", "review_text": "Chances are, you've found this keyboard after reading a number of Reddit threads or watching a review or 2 on Youtube, and I can confirm they're all very correct to recommend this keyboard.
It's kind of obvious that it's not trying to be high-end, as evidenced by the all plastic build, basic and other creature-comforts that are left out, like volume knobs and little near-useless LED screens, but it is still a solid, well built keyboard with a decent-enough feature set.
But, it's a keyboard, so if we're being real, its the tactile feel of typing on this thing along with it's really nice, satisfying "creamy" sound (at least that's what I've heard it called, though I still don't quite get why) that makes you want mechanical keyboard like this and this one does the thing real well while also looking pretty dang nice at the same time (I got the gray gradient version with side-printed keycaps. The battery life using the included USB 2.4G wireless dongle is exceptionally good and it also has RGB backlighting with 20 preprogrammed lighting modes, if you're into that thing, but I've got it set to a static color and it looks good enough for me.
All of that at this price point makes this a really, really, really good option and one that I can absolutely recommend.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Angela", "review_title": "Amazing, and truly worth the price.", "review_text": "It's a truly amazing keyboard, it feels great, looks great, and sounds great. I have only one issue with it, it's loud, but that's only an issue at night. The ergonomics feel pretty good, and the switches are very nice and responsive. Everything feels high quality, especially for this price. Very worth it and affordable.
The backlight is a nice touch, it can be disabled and enabled, along with changing the color and speed.
Note:
"Mom if you're seeing this, I wrote this review" -your son.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Wiaan", "review_title": "Amazing keyboard for the price", "review_text": "This keyboard sounds even better than the reviews claim. Before buying, I came across a few comments suggesting that some of the internal padding had been removed or that the overall quality had declined as the keyboard became more popular. After using it myself, I can confidently say that those concerns were unfounded.
The build quality is excellent, the typing experience is incredibly satisfying, and the switches feel fantastic. Every keypress sounds and feels premium, making it a joy to use for both work and gaming.
So far, I’ve only tested the 2.4GHz wireless mode, so I can’t comment on the wired or Bluetooth performance. However, based on my experience, I have no hesitation recommending it.
For the price, this keyboard offers outstanding value. It was absolutely worth the wait, especially considering I ordered it from the US and had it shipped to South Africa.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "William Urling", "review_title": "The best value for a budget keyboard, hands down.", "review_text": "This keyboard has been an absolute dream, and the price cannot be beat. It uses bsun switches (I'm honestly not sure which, I've done some digging but can't find them), of which I got the linear version. These switches are nice, there is no noticeable scratch, a crisp bottom out, and the stabilizers are actually silent with no rattle or ticking. There is a variety of foam included, but they leave a bit of room in the case which keeps the board from sounding muted. There are NO SCREWS, so modding this thing is a breeze (might need a small flathead tho) and you have a lot of options straight out of the box. It also comes with a hotswap board, so you can lube the switches (already lubed, but do what you want) or change them out entirely. There are also FLIPPY FEET (2 STAGE!!) so you can adjust your typing angle. I have heard people complain about the software that comes with the board, but it turns out it is fully compatible with the Signal RGB app. Now I can assign any pattern I want, even outside of the presets! The lighting is very prominent since the LEDs are south-facing. 3 of the lights do not work in the software, but they are on the edge of the board with the modifier keys so they are not noticeable.
My ONLY gripe is that the keycaps are not very durable. I have been using mine for a few months now and the tops of the WASD keys are starting to become shiny and smoother. These are likely not PBT, but they are a very thick ABS so the sound stays deeper and fuller. However, a PBT set from a name brand manufacturer costs more than this entire keyboard, so this is an incredibly minor complaint.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Billlydee", "review_title": "Comfortable, creamy sound, easy set up.", "review_text": "Set up was a breeze, simply plug in. It charges in a few hours.
This keyboard is really nice. I like the “creamy” sound other viewers have described. A VERY light touch is all you need to type. I won’t say it’s sensitive, it just requires a light touch of each key. That is something I need to get used to.
I have a laptop set up on a riser, and needed a keyboard that will fit in the small space beneath it. This was my choice after reviewing MANY keyboards. I also wanted a laptop with raised keys, a mechanical keyboard. I like the “old school” feel of it.
Weight: it’s heavy. I won’t be traveling with it, so that doesn’t matter to me. But I love the heaviness of it. Feels secure in its spot.
Ergonomics: there are two levels if you want to change the angle. Three is you count not using the little feet at the back. I also have a padded hand/wrist rest for extra comfort (NOT INCLUDED) but the keyboard itself is comfortable to use.
Color: I would have preferred black to match my desk accessories and laptop, or blue my favorite color. I went for the least expensive option as the color doesn’t change the effectiveness of the device.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Gabriel Velázquez", "review_title": "Buen sonido y calidad por el precio, pero software y patas mejorables", "review_text": "El teclado superó mis expectativas en lo esencial: sonido “thock” muy placentero, pulsaciones firmes y tres modos de conexión que funcionan sin problema. La construcción se siente sólida; el plástico es grueso y limpio al tacto, de mejor calidad que en otros modelos de su rango.
Puntos a favor:
Excelente sensación y respuesta lineal.
Sonido grave-cremoso desde fábrica, sin necesidad de mods.
Muy buen valor por el precio: se acerca a prestaciones “custom” de gamas más altas.
Puntos a mejorar:
El software de administración fue inútil en dos PC. La página es confusa, y aunque el teclado fue reconocido, no ofrecía opciones reales de configuración.
La parte trasera utiliza un plástico más sencillo, y las gomas antideslizantes están pegadas con cinta doble faz que comenzó a despegarse desde el primer día. Me preocupa que se pierdan o necesiten ser reemplazadas pronto.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Diwakar", "review_title": "Fantastic Keybaord", "review_text": "Excellent Product", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Billy", "review_title": "BEST KEYBOARD I HAVE EVER USED. WORTH EVERY PENNY.", "review_text": "Honestly, I am absolutely blown away with the quality of this kisnt KN85, it's hands down the best keyboard I have ever owned. First of all, the sound quality of the key click is insane, this thing is so thocky with the bsun switches, PBT double shot key caps, gasket mounts and multiple layers of dampening foam/silicone, genuinely such a pleasure to type with. It is even hot-swappable if you want to change or upgrade your switches. The battery life is amazing, first use never charged out of the box lasted over a full week of heavy daily use.
I find it very hard to find any fault with this keyboard whatsoever. One note is that the LED's are south-facing, so shine-through backlit keycaps won't work, I like double-shot caps for the thock, so this doesn't bother me one bit. But seriously, I have never been so happy to be typing at my desk. It has changed my whole experience. I watch reviews of £200-£500 keyboards, and I still think this is better.
All I will say is get it fast, as prices are constantly rising due to demand.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Ontarioo", "review_title": "It's really solid", "review_text": "looks and feels amazing, setup was easy and battery is lasting along time which is great. but the sound of the keyboard is so creamy, it really does sound like a premium keyboard. I also love the beige color scheme its very clean yet retro and the letters are bolded and of course its not a lousy 60% so you can enjoy all the key functions without having to press FN all the time", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "KM", "review_title": "Better than expected", "review_text": "Awesome keyboard that punches above its weight. Stock switches are louder than I'd like, but hey it's a custom keyboard, so just swap them out easily for anything you like. For the price it's great keyboard. ONLY major issue is I like separate numpad controllers (I put these on the right of my mouse so it's quicker) but Kisnt only make these seperate numpads for the two other colour schemes that exist. The beige and green scheme is missing.", "review_rating": ""}]

Title: Razer BlackWidow V4 X Mechanical Gaming Keyboard, Yellow Switches, Black
Description: YELLOW MECHANICAL LINEAR SWITCHES: With zero distance between actuation and reset points at 1.2mm and only 45g of force required — enjoy instant, rapid-fire inputs that are just as quiet thanks to built-in sound dampeners
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Hurting", "review_title": "It's a good board", "review_text": "Ok, so after spending a couple weeks with this board I can tell you-
A couple of things I wasn't really aware of-
1) Just how much pressure I'm used to applying at rest on keys
2) How much I relied on outside esc and ctrl keys for orientation
These keys are very sensitive compared to the old BW I've used for years. I've been accidentally entering a lot of keystrokes at rest. They are very quiet and soft stroking compared to the green switches in the older Black Widow I've retired. So if you want clicks, feedback or resistance look elsewhere. Believe it or not my main hesitation for getting this board was the outside left row of programmable keys. I was afraid that it would be in the way and get confused with my escape and control keys, which yes has been very challenging to get used to, but it's no fault of the board itself knowing what I was getting. I pulled up all those caps on that row and replaced with wider pudding caps for brighter distinction. Programed those keys to mirror their neighbors, esc ,Ctrl etc so that when an erroneous keystroke is made it should at least still be the function I was looking for, albeit orientation may be off from wasd. So anyway I'm having to look down a lot more at the keyboard and retraining my mind to orient off the *F key", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Scott C", "review_title": "Durable and well built. Survived a liquid disaster.", "review_text": "I have the green switch version.
Durable and Chroma lighting is excellent. Put O rings in the keys to dampen slightly. Key feeling and clicks are a matter of personal preference.
Spilled coffee on this one twice. I thought the keyboard was toast after the last disaster spill. Keys weren't functioning and the leds were out. I took it apart and rinsed it out the affected areas heavily with alcohol. Blew the liquid out with compressed air/compressor. Works fine now.
After taking it apart I could see how good the quality was. Keyboard backplate is actually solid metal.
2 screws under the top two rubber foot pads. Careful, the pads tear easily.
18+- screws under the keys. Remove the keys to find them all.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Matt T.", "review_title": "Best Keyboard I've Had", "review_text": "Zero complaints, satisfying sound, a lot of cool features. Very satisying feeling when typing, not loud or clunky at all. You can tell the quality of the build by the weigh it feels and it's weight. I love also the volume wheel, so cool!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Connor Nanney", "review_title": "Great Keyboard, would buy again", "review_text": "Had it for a bit over a week now and it's been great. I originally had the Razer blackwidow V1 with the green clicks switches and it was great the thing finally crapped out on me a few weeks ago. The thing lasted me forever, was super durable and felt very responsive. My biggest complaint was it was hard to clean. So I decided to go with the newest version and try the Yellow switches. I didn't like the softer yellow switches at first but have come to like them and this keyboard solved the cleaning issue. My biggest problem was actually the Macro keys on the left hand side. With my old keyboard I used the edge of they keyboard to orient my hand without looking when gaming, this makes it hard to do that because my fingers end up on the macro keys. I've started to retrain myself to position properly but it wasn't easy. Other than that this keyboard is fantastic.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "James", "review_title": "Works great, looks great", "review_text": "Awesome keyboard!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Angel", "review_title": "Solid Keyboard", "review_text": "Fun RGB lighting, fully customizable colors within the Razer lighting program. Lighting program is easy to use with plenty of tutorials on installation. Can customize individual keys for different lighting when pressed. Extra macro buttons on the left will take some getting used to, but just imagine what all you can assign them as. Solid keyboard in terms of weight, back wings to lift up to have it at a slight angle. Keycaps nice and solid quality. These are soft and bubbly sounding in my opinion, not sharp and clicky. In prior experience with Razer, the price is a bit up there, but I would wager its worth it. Received on September 28th, 2025; will check back after a while to update review if needed.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Kevin T.", "review_title": "Shoddy Construction, Unresponsive key issues", "review_text": "Before I got this keyboard, I was using the 2016 edition razer blackwidow ultimate. That keyboard still works perfectly, and the only problem I had with it was that the keyboard was LOUD as heck.
Enter the blackwidow v4 x with yellow switches. At first i was extremely happy with the look, feel, and materials of the keyboard, it felt very premium, and the keys were MUCH quieter.
I bought it in December of 2023. By March 2024 I noticed an issue with the "P" key being unresponsive. Meaning when you press the key, there was a chance of it not registering the keypress. So if you press the key 10 times, it may only display about 5 or 6 times. Not that bad for gaming since the "P" key is hardly used. However when typing it could get very annoying. I attached a video showing me trying to press the button 3 times, followed by a space, then the button 3 times, then a space etc. You can clearly see it does not register the keypress quite often.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "ben", "review_title": "great keyboard", "review_text": "absolutely love it great keyboard. really good for the price lighting on the rgb is amazing. so far it feels really durable.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "mitesh", "review_title": "Best Keyboard", "review_text": "Fantastic keyboard as per my choice and also this works well. The package was all good at the time I recieved it. All items were there and the experience is amazing.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Steven", "review_title": "way better quality than expected", "review_text": "I've had my fair share of gaming keyboards but this one in particular feels great and was way better quality than expected.
It is relatively quiet for a gaming keyboard and has excellent tactile feedback.
The backlight is clean and vibrant as well.
My only complaint would be the macro buttons on the left of the keyboard, but only because I am personally not used to it from previous keyboards.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Lonely Sickoz", "review_title": "Muy buena calidad", "review_text": "Es el primer teclado que compro.
Es el estilo contemporáneo.
Estoy feliz con mi compa no se siente barata hasta la cuerda usb muy reciente.
Las luces son muy lindas.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Majid soaimel", "review_title": "Don't prefer Razer, but it's ZZZ so I made an exception", "review_text": "It's super clicky which I hate and it's not swappable which is absurd. The RGB is very inaccurate when setting up but when you do, it looks nice enough. I still prefer my KDA Logitech G Pro keyboard but I got this because it's miyabi <3 the keys are very nice to the touch, although I hate that the macro buttons are on the left, they're messing up with my muscle memory but I can get used to them. The keyboard is metal, cool to the touch, and heavy.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Rodrigo B.", "review_title": "Una edición muy bonita", "review_text": "Los switches son un poco ruidosos pero aún así me gustó mucho el diseño y la calidad del teclado.", "review_rating": ""}]

Title: RisoPhy Mechanical Gaming Keyboard, RGB 104 Keys Ultra-Slim LED Backlit USB Wired Keyboard with Blue Switch, Durable Abs Keycaps/Anti-Ghosting/Spill-Resistant Computer Keyboard for PC Mac Xbox Gamer
Description: 【Mechanical Keyboard: Responsive BLue Switches】RisoPhy PC keyboard features clicky keys which offer you higher accuracy and quicker response with an enjoyable click sound when typing.This keyboard is more comfortable to type on since it features deeper key travel,greater feedback,and more space between keys.For those who prefer keyboards with a more tactile and "clicky" feel,our keyboard with BLUE switches is a nice choice.
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "jaycha2", "review_title": "★★★★★ Great first impressions!", "review_text": "Just received my RisoPhy RGB Mechanical Gaming Keyboard and I'm already impressed! Unboxing was smooth — everything was well packaged and arrived in perfect condition.
Right out of the gate, the mechanical switches feel fantastic — satisfying and responsive with great tactile feedback. Typing this review on it now and it already feels way better than my old membrane keyboard.
