Title: SteelSeries USB Apex 5 Hybrid Mechanical Gaming Keyboard – Per-Key RGB Illumination – Aircraft Grade Aluminum Alloy Frame – OLED Smart Display (Hybrid Blue Switch)
Description: Hybrid blue mechanical gaming switches – The tactile click of a blue mechanical switch plus a smooth membrane – guaranteed for 20 million keypresses
Category: Electronics,Computers & Accessories,Computer Accessories & Peripherals,Keyboards, Mice & Accessories,Keyboards
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Barbara Smoyer", "review_title": "Great Keyboard and Great Features!", "review_text": "This keyboard is probably the best one I've ever had. It is built so well. It is made mostly of some sort of aluminum. It does not bend at all and it just feels very nice. I have had a keyboard that was so cheap that it bent even when I was typing normally (I don't type very hard), so this was a nice change. The metal volume dial is very high quality, and yet again, just feels well-built. There is also a little button that controls 4 things. It will pause and play your music, skip to the next song, go to the previous song, and open up menus in the OLED display. The OLED screen is very nice. It could be a little brighter, and the larger pixels make it harder to display certain things. But, what makes up for that is that with the program you can install, you can download apps that will change what the screen says. My 2 favorites are Discord and System Monitor. They RGB lighting is really nice. Each light can be its own color and with the program, you can make your own lighting configurations. The keys sound very nice. They are clicky, but too clicky. They are also easy to press, but not so easy that I could see myself accidentally pressing one. It also comes with a wrist rest. It magnetically attaches and feels very smooth and high quality. Overall this keyboard just feels very premium and super high quality. I would recommend it to someone who wants a good keyboard with some very nice features from a good brand and does not mind spending the premium cost.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Camilo Salazar", "review_title": "SteelSeries Apex 5 – Almost a 5-Star Keyboard, but Not Quite (4.76 on My Scale)", "review_text": "The SteelSeries Apex 5 left a strong impression. It’s a well-built keyboard with some excellent features and clever design choices. The cable is thick, long, and even has a nice touch — the SteelSeries logo on the USB plug. The RGB effects are top-notch, with smooth transitions both on keypress and when idle. I was genuinely excited about all of this... until I noticed what was missing. And for me, that’s a big deal.
Let’s break it down.😁
### What Makes It (Almost) 5 Stars – The Good:😃
- Excellent Media Controls: The volume wheel is fantastic: easy to reach, smooth to use, and includes a click-to-mute function. The menu button also works similarly to the playback controls found on many headsets with built-in microphones or hands-free kits. Super convenient.
- Onboard Controls – No Software Needed: You can manage brightness, RGB colors, effects, profiles, and more — all from the keyboard itself. No software required. Only macros can’t be directly viewed or edited in menu, which is a small detail worth noting.
- Smart OLED Display: It shows the status of Num Lock, Caps Lock, Scroll Lock, and whether the Windows key is disabled. Very handy (though there’s a small catch — more on that below).", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Ken", "review_title": "Outstanding, with a possible caveat", "review_text": "Five months into owning this keyboard and it's easily my favorite keyboard I've ever had. Reasonably heavy so it easily stays in place even banging out page after page of typing documents, but doesn't feel like a slab of lead. The entire assembly is well put together; the keyboard has a nice, satin texture across the body and the keys, which feels great under the fingers, though it does show some oils more easily so I recommend regular cleaning/wipedowns.
This keyboard uses an odd hybrid system between mechanical/membrane, some proprietary/trade secret Steelseries BS, though honestly, if this wasn't pointed out to me after the fact I probably wouldn't have caught on. This uses cherry stems and switches, and the keys are naturally a cherry profile, so finding aftermarket replacements/decorative keycaps is easy as well. The keys feel responsive and clicky, delightfully so, when gaming or typing for general purpose. But there's a catch; it's a hybrid, so not truly mechanical. It does feel very good, but I have concerns that the membrane will wear down in time as opposed to a true blue mechanical keyboard, which will stay responsive and snappy for a lesser eternity where membranes begin to show wear after a year of heavy use. Time will tell.
The lighting is phenomenal - the LEDs are bright, responsive, and have great color depth and range compared to a lot of RGB hardware out there. You can use Steelseries' own software to customize and program this keyboard outside of the 5 existing presets saved onto the board's memory, but you can also use other third-party RGB control software like SignalRGB.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Ibrahim Amir", "review_title": "Great entry mechanical keyboard with solid feel and comfort", "review_text": "I bought this for my 14-year-old, and it’s been a great keyboard for both gaming and schoolwork. The hybrid switches feel clicky and responsive without being overly loud, and the RGB is bright and customizable enough for their setup. The included wrist rest adds real comfort and doesn’t slide around. No issues with software or macros so far. It’s a well-rounded keyboard that feels more premium than its price suggests.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Raymond Ligenza", "review_title": "Awesome!", "review_text": "Excellent individual RGB keys. Cool but small LCD screen (But it displays my CPU temp, so I'm happy). Volume control is super handy, and it's compatible with SignalRGB. Not to mention this keyboards clicks sound amazing! If you're into the old school keyboard sound.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "James Kitelinger", "review_title": "Nice keyboard - Amazon Refurbished just sucks", "review_text": "I have only had this keyboard for a few days at the time of this review, but from what I can tell it is a solidly built keyboard with a nice feel and decently responsive keys.
I did have to knock off a star though as the keyboard I received was in poor condition with two of the keys having keypress detection issues. This however was NOT the fault of SteelSeries as I bought this one from Amazon Refurbished.
Do NOT buy this keyboard from Amazon Refurbished. They do only the bare minimum to make the keyboard presentable, and do not open it to check the internals before shipping it. Or else they would have seen the gunk inside that was causing the key press detection issue.
Thankfully, user maintenance was easy. Simple matter of taking off the key caps, taking out the cover screws, and the mainboard screws. Then I was able to clean it with a little alcohol and reassemble it. Works like it was new. Just didn't expect that I would have to be the one doing the refurbishing on day one. But that's why I gave it 4 stars, pretty easy to perform user maintenance on it to ensure that it continues to function. Which boggles me why Amazon didn't do that.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "NonDescript", "review_title": "Great keybaord!", "review_text": "Got this to replace a $250 Razor keyboard that went out after four years with largely only work-related use. I have keyboards from the '90s that still work. Razor customer service didn't even respond to me. That being said, I'm happy with this one. Less than half the price and works just as well. So much, I bough one for my son as well!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Triston", "review_title": "Amazing keyboard!", "review_text": "Amazing! It has many cool features and sounds amazing. It’s full sized too so you don’t miss out on any extra keys.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Daniel", "review_title": "Mi primer teclado mecánico. Totalmente satisfecho", "review_text": "Excelentes materiales de construcción, amplias opciones para configurar prácticamente cualquier cosa del teclado y gran comodidad.
Pasé de un teclado de membrana "gamer" Logitech G213 a este SteelSeries Apex 5 y la diferencia puede notarse. Desde los efectos RGB ampliamente configurables a través del software SteelSeries GG hasta el tacto en las teclas y el reposamuñecas (que está hecho de un material de plástico suave al tacto), todo es súper cómodo y de gran calidad.
Algo que me gusta bastante de este teclado es su pequeña pantalla OLED en la esquina superior derecha, que puede configurarse con algún dibujo, algún GIF o con alguna de las integraciones que tiene con algunos juegos o programas. Yo particularmente la uso para monitorear mi sistema y ver la temperatura a la que se encuentra mi CPU y GPU de manera rápida y sencilla sin tener que ejecutar MSI Afterburner o RivaTuner SS. Sin embargo, tal y como vi en la propia página del producto y en algunas reseñas en YouTube, se podía visualizar la canción que estuvieras escuchando en el momento, pero por lo que pude investigar esto solo es posible si usas TIDAL y bueno, yo utilizo Spotify, por lo que esto no me agradó tanto.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "ellie whilding", "review_title": "Everything is good about this", "review_text": "The keyboard is amazing. It has per key illumination which the software is very cool with.
It gets recognised by signal rgb software so it syncs everything together.
The feel is good it has mechanical clicks with membrane so doesn't feel like your bottoming out the keys.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Ian Tyracek", "review_title": "Very Satisfied", "review_text": "I wanted a kind of middle road price RGB keyboard and I am in love with this one. The keys feel very satisfying and loud and clicky. The RGB support is great, I use signalRGB so that was a major selling point that it worked for that. I do wish it had better side controls for audio and even though you can pause spotify or whatever with the top right button it only pauses your last application which can be anything so that can be a bit annoying. The scroll wheel does work well for volume control though.
Overall I do like it a lot, good colour and feel. Recommend for those who want something nice but dont want to drop 200", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "plewpy", "review_title": "good keyboard", "review_text": "nice switches, almost cant feel the rubber dome, the hand rest feels great", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Youssef Gh", "review_title": "Awesome.", "review_text": "Never knew what I was missing out on before I got this.
So. Worth. It.", "review_rating": ""}]

Title: AULA WIN68 HE Mechanical Gaming Keyboard 60%, Hall Effect Magnetic Switch, Fast Trigger Mode Adjustable Actuation, 8000Hz Polling Rate, RGB Backlit, Wired Black Keyboard for Laptop/PC Gamer
Description: Fast Trigger Gaming Keyboard: AULA WIN68 HE magnetic gaming keyboard offers an industry-leading 8,000Hz polling rate and 8x faster response time than traditional mechanical keyboard. Combined with ultra-low latency (0.3ms), it ensures your commands take effect instantly, giving you an edge in the game. Reviews: [{"reviewer_name": "MachinaBuyer", "review_title": "Budget HE keyboard that gives you all you need...", "review_text": "AULA WIN68 HE is my first ever HE keyboard, after years of being in the world of mechanical keyboards and exclusively favoring the brown switch (tactile) I always watched many videos and people praising HE keyboards and the edge they give to you in gaming primarily. We all know of the famed Wooting 60 HE which started this trend in gaming world both the price and being only 60% give's it only a small and competitive market for a few individuals that can afford it or need it for professional e-Sports. As primarily a single-player gamer I was blow away with how much HE switches changes your experience of playing and gives you for the first time ever something that gamepads had over keyboards, and that is you don't need to push the key all the way for it work, both only a slight push fulfils the given command that you want (MMOs and racing games benefit from this the most). The web software is one of the best features of this keyboard and it allows you to customize every single key however you want it, every key supports rapid trigger as well as customizing the dead zone as well as primarily the sensitivity of the keys. The standard version that I have allows you to customize the sensitivity from 0.8mm to larger if you prefer (default being 1.70mm, while mechanical boards clock at 2.1mm). Keyboard is hot swappable and you can change your magnetic switches really easily. Brightness and RGB is also good with no complaints in that department (you can customize it in the web software). The build quality is also good and think that board was upgraded to PBT switches since when typing on them the feel sandy and rough, sound quality is quite since magnetic switches are linear switches (both better in every way), and the keyboard is wired only which I prefer since I am using it on my personal PC and have no need to use it elsewhere. HE keyboards are definitely the future and every professional or enthusiast e-Sport gamer simply must have this keyboard because it gives them and edge in every way that mechanical keyboard simply cannot give at the moment! I recommended this board for anybody who is on the fence over coming to the HE world.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "wilnam", "review_title": "best gaming keyboard", "review_text": "feels nice and colors are great super durable and size is amazing not too heavy and typing feels so smooth and connects perfectly like any other keyboard love the fact that you can change how little you have to press in order for it to register. 10/10", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Alexander", "review_title": "Best for gamers or HE keyb enthusiasts", "review_text": "Very silky smooth, sounds absolutely amazing and feels even better, the software drivers were kinda hard to find n looked like a scam but were not and work perfectly, though you don't need the software for much unless you care about the actuation points and all that special stuff, which you probably do since you're getting a HE keyb, came with everything in box everything works, very high quality feel its heavier (In a good way) than my old keyb I bought for around 60 usd. Got just the standard black keyb but the rgbs all show through the keycaps really good and none of them are buggy or broken. All in all its very worth it if you're a gamer or just care about hall effect keybs in general. It's a 60% so you obv don't have all the keys of a 100% but it's definitely good for saving space. But that's why I mainly recommend to gamers or people who are looking for specific features.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Jillian", "review_title": "Great Quality", "review_text": "Perfect for Gamers! My son has a 200.00 keyboard and actually prefers this one. Great price and quick clicks.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Austin", "review_title": "Solid Build, Great Sound, and Impressive Lighting Options", "review_text": "I\u2019ve been using the AULA WIN68 HE keyboard for a while now, and it\u2019s been a great experience overall. The compact size is small enough to save desk space but not so small that it feels restrictive\u2014everything is still right where you need it. The function key functionality is seamless, making it easy to access all the extra commands without breaking your flow. The typing sound is crisp and satisfying without being too loud, and the build quality is excellent\u2014solid and heavy enough that it won\u2019t slide around, even if you accidentally bump it. The RGB lighting is another standout, offering a wide range of patterns and configurations to match any setup. One thing I\u2019m still unsure about is the \u201cdifferent switches\u201d option in the software\u2014it\u2019s visible, but I\u2019m not entirely certain what it changes, if anything. Considering the overall quality, sound, build, lighting, and features, this keyboard delivers an impressive experience for such a budget-friendly price.\nOverall, I highly recommend this keyboard to anybody looking for a budget-friendly gaming keyboard!\nI've attached a picture with my Logitech G305 mouse for a scale reference.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "James", "review_title": "amazing, good inputs", "review_text": "very nice, good software, nice switches with nice sound and inputs are extremely fast and good, went very good with my black setup.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Adam", "review_title": "very good", "review_text": "bought for my nephew since his keyboard broke and he loves it compared to my wooting 80 he which is a $200 keyboard and it somewhat feels the same with the accusation and rapid tap, it obviously feels a little cheaper bc it is!! if your balling on a budget and wanna save $160 buy this keyboard it\u2019s definitely worth it, the software is really good to be explained it and has all the same choices almost", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Leonardo Valenzuela", "review_title": "Keys acting as if they are being pressed down", "review_text": "They keyboard is good for sure the software is pretty solid i was a little confused by some of it but im sure its a snoop more learn more kind of thing. the feel is like any keyboard youd expect the sound honestly out of any keyboard ive had its amount the best sounding pretty crisp to me. however after months i had moments it would act up pretty weird. Title: RK ROYAL KLUDGE R98 Pro Wired Mechanical Keyboard, 96% Creamy Gaming Keyboard RGB Backlit with Number Pad and Volume Knob, Gasket Mount, MDA Profile PBT Keycaps, Hot Swappable Pre-lubed Linear Switch
Description: 【Gasket Mount Gaming Keyboard with Number Pad】: Computer keyboard adopts 98 keys layout design, retaining numpad, arrow keys and most functions, saving your desktop space and making it more suitable for gaming and work. Five layers sound-absorbing foam to ensure thocky feeling and creamy sounding for you
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Akshar", "review_title": "As per Description!!", "review_text": "I’ve been using the RK Royal Kludge R98 Pro for a little over a week, and I’m honestly impressed with how much value this keyboard delivers. The moment you take it out of the box, it feels solid and well-built definitely not your typical budget keyboard.
Typing Experience (5/5)
The gasket mount design combined with the pre‑lubed linear switches makes typing incredibly smooth and quiet. It has that “creamy” feel everyone talks about. No pinging, no rattling just clean, soft keystrokes. The MDA profile PBT keycaps are thick, durable, and comfortable to type on.
Design & Layout (5/5)
I love the 96% layout. It saves desk space but still includes a full number pad, which I use constantly for work. The addition of the volume knob is a nice touch and works great for quick adjustments.
RGB & Customization (4.5/5)
The RGB is bright, vibrant, and offers a ton of effects. Customizing it is easy once you get familiar with the shortcuts. I only wish the software was a bit more intuitive, but it’s definitely not a deal‑breaker.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Liliyanna", "review_title": "Amazing gaming keyboard", "review_text": "So, i dont usually write reviews, but i felt i had to for this keyboards. the creamy clicks are AMAZING (its my first time having it so im super impressed.) the tiny screen is actually pretty simple and easy to use, you can customize the backlight color and style, speed, etc. the knob works perfect. feels great. it came with extra keys, a usb-c to plug in if you prefer wired, and a key remover. everything feels amazing, very high quality. its obviously not 10 pounds, but carries some heft that feels super secure. its got little folded stands to prop your keyboard up if desired, which i think is super nice. i love the color variety (i got the brown, for reference.), it can be hard finding a nice keyboard that is still stylish and pretty. im extremely satisfied, especially with the price being only 70 usd for this nice of a keyboard. i still have yet to use it, but im pretty confident it will be nice. ill update if anything happens!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Eric", "review_title": "I am surprised how much I actually like this keyboard", "review_text": "I recently purchased this item a couple of weeks ago and so I think it was a good purchase. First of all, they keyboard is super smooth and because of the switches, you do hear some clicks but they're not that loud, just enough to be satisfying. The product feels well-crafted with quality in mind. The keyboard stands; are the perfect size, not freakish large so typing for long periods of time is comfortable. I also like how they send you the "end" key in the box so if you don't like the volume knob, you can put the "end" key back in. I type 80 words a minute, especially when I am writing programs, I pleased on how well the keys on this board respond and the entire feeling of when a key is pressed. When I type superfast on things that are super important, I don't want my keyboard to fail me.
Now, there are a few things I don't really like about it but overall, like I said, this is a great keyboard.
- The volume knob: Hey, it works but personally, I feel that it is too close to the "pgdn" key so you really can't grip it like a knob. I kind of wished it had groves or something on the dial making it easier to turn. Right now, I just got to try and turn it little by little by spinning the know from the top down to the "-" key. That's about all the room you got.
- Key position: This one is more of my fault. I am more used to full sized keyboards and not the space saving ones with less keys. The part that messes me up is where the arrows, shift, and enter is all smushed together. If this might also, be you, check out the S98 model instead.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "walkebe", "review_title": "Absolutely Impressed!", "review_text": "I upgraded my home gaming setup with this keyboard after considerable research, and it’s been a joy to use for both gaming and typing.
Strengths:
Premium typing experience: The pre-lubed cream linear switches and gasket mount deliver a “thocky” feel and satisfyingly smooth keystrokes. Typing and gaming are both quiet and comfortable, with five layers of foam dampening any hollow sounds.
Customization: The included software lets me remap keys, create macros, and adjust more than 20 dynamic RGB lighting modes quickly. I loved being able to easily tweak the look and functionality.

[{"reviewer_name": "aya holland", "review_title": "LOVE my first mechanical keyboard", "review_text": "This is the first mechanical keyboard that i got and i absolutely love it. I did some research before getting a keyboard since i wanted something of a good quality but was prepared to drop $100+ on it. Very pleased with the quality of t his one - it feels very sturdy, the keys have just enough resistance to effortless typing.

It also allows pairing with 3 devices (and switch with a brass of a button, well, 2 buttons but u get it) via Bluetooth and it’s very convenient since i can use it with my computer, iPad and steam deck.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Aub", "review_title": "Smooth and Satisfying Mechanical Keyboard", "review_text": "This keyboard has a great feel right out of the box. It feels really sturdy and it’s honestly one of my favorite desk purchases! 5/5 ⭐️", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Kay", "review_title": "Amazing keyboard, sturdy, lovely sound", "review_text": "i am very picky about my keyboards but this is the second AULA keyboard i have gotten and i am in love once again. the videos and pictures don’t do it justice it looks and sounds amazing, i love creamy / thocky sounding keyboards and this one is perfect.
the resistance on the keys is great, the sound is great, the whole thing is great so i definitely recommend getting this if you’re thinking about it, it is worth the money 100% it is so nice to type on and i use the usb connector ( my cats are going through a wire chewing stage) and its great.
i also love the adjustability of the keyboard, i always have the back end sit up higher, the material is solid and it feels super weighted which i love. there are a bunch of different color options i didnt show all of them in the video but i normally have mine on white or off.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "alfie", "review_title": "AULA F75 Review Glacial Blue Reaper Switches", "review_text": "I’ve been using the AULA F75 keyboard as my main keyboard, and it has been a great upgrade from my previous one, especially considering the price. Title: Razer Huntsman V3 HE Magnetic Mini 65% 8KHz Wired Gaming Keyboard
Description: PRECISION FOR COMPETITIVE GAMING – Dominate FPS games and esports tournaments with Razer Hall Effect Magnetic Switches featuring Rapid Trigger and adjustable 0.1-4.0 mm actuation for faster reactions, cleaner movement inputs, and personalized control
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Pablo Ladino", "review_title": "A huge upgrade from my BlackWidow V3", "review_text": "I honestly didn’t expect to like this keyboard this much. I upgraded from a Razer BlackWidow V3, and the difference is immediately noticeable.
The magnetic switches feel incredibly smooth and responsive, and being able to adjust the actuation point and use Rapid Trigger is a game changer for competitive gaming. Movement feels much more precise, especially in Fortnite. The keyboard also feels extremely well built and premium.
What I really like is that it isn’t only great for gaming. For everyday use, studying, and programming, I can switch to a normal profile and it feels just as good to type on.
I was a little skeptical at first because I was already happy with my BlackWidow V3, but after using this one, I don’t think I could go back to a traditional mechanical keyboard.
If you’re coming from a regular mechanical keyboard, this is a serious upgrade. Absolutely love it so far. 🔥", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "HikerBrian", "review_title": "Incredible for coding, even better for gaming,", "review_text": "This one gets reviewed from two angles. As a professional software engineer I live by the quality of my keyboard and have been opinionated about keyboards for more than 20 years, so I ran this as my daily driver for a week to test it out. It was quiet, consistent, and responsive. Despite the gaming branding, this is probably the best tenkeyless keyboard I've ever typed on. Turn the lighting off and it can be dropped onto any office desk without getting a second glance. The high quality PBT keycaps have a texture that doesn't go slick and greasy, and they shouldn't shine up the way ABS does after a few months of heavy use. The switches are factory lubed with a dense foam layer underneath, so there's no hollow plastic rattle and no metallic ping. It's also not the clicking like you get from mechanical switches. It's a low, dull sound that doesn't get annoying in a quiet room or on a call. The adjustable actuation mattered more than I expected for office use. Setting it deeper than a gamer would means you stop firing off accidental characters when your fingers graze the home row, which is something that makes most fast-actuation boards frustrating for long-form writing and code. The aluminum top gives it a solid build, so it doesn't flex or walk across the desk, and the detachable USB-C cable means a longer lifespan.
After my week ended I handed it to my teenage son, the gamer, and I really don't think I'm getting it back. He found things I never would have. Rapid Trigger resets the key the instant it starts to rise instead of waiting for a fixed point, which he says completely changes counter-strafing. Snap Tap prioritizes whichever direction key you pressed most recently, so pressing A while holding D doesn't leave you standing there. Dynamic Keystroke lets a single key fire up to four different actions depending on how far down you press it, and Snap Flex assigns one action on press and a different one on release. He set up a key that peeks a corner on a light press and pulls back on release. I didn't even know keyboards did that, but he's raving about it. The 8000Hz polling means it reports to the PC eight times more often than a standard board. He swears he can feel it. I'm skeptical it's perceptible, but he's the one winning matches. All of the tuning lives in the browser based software, which allows you to adjust lighting, actuation and keybinds without installing anything.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "NhutDuong", "review_title": "Good", "review_text": "Good", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "AmazonReviewer", "review_title": "Love the design and layout, and the HE switches feels great! I also love the keycaps texture!", "review_text": "I have multiple razer keyboards from down to the 2010 black widow which is still going strong, and a few newer ones from last year and I love them, but when I saw this new huntsman V3 HE 65% keyboard I wanted to see how it was.
Build quality is very solid, it has a nice looking aluminum plate which is very sturdy and does not bend when I push hard on it, and it has a decent amount of weight to it which is not too light or too heavy. I also like that it has dual stage feet which most 65% keyboards do without with them, and I like the way they made the USB port going in the case so the cable can sit flush in it, which does help prevent wearing out the USB Type C port or getting broken.
And it feels really good while gaming or typing on it with the new HE magnetic switches, they are really smooth and has a nice clacky sound profile and it is very responsive, the PBT keycaps feels really good and I really do love the grippy texture they have on them that my fingers do not slide off them when gaming for long sessions, and they are shine through legends and they are very easy to see in the dark.
The rgb lighting looks really good which I have to say Razer always had the best RGB lighting in my opinion, which there is tons of effects to choose from and to make with the Synapse software, only thing I do notice is the backlighting is not really bright because they did choose to use a diffuser on the switches were the LED are at and the switches have a frosted housing to them, but I really not picky about backlighting on keyboards so it's not an issue for me, but it still looks really good. And you do have to use the software to change the lighting because it can't be done on the keyboard itself, only the brightness can be done on the keyboard itself, but a workaround with that is using the onboard memory which has up to 6 profiles which that can be used for different lighting effects and it works good that way.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "MK", "review_title": "Razer’s Hall Effect Switches Are a Major Improvement", "review_text": "Razer has made adjustable-actuation keyboards before, but its previous analog Huntsman models relied on optical switches. This is its first real move into the Hall effect keyboard space, and the switch change is not just a spec-sheet distinction. These new magnetic switches feel noticeably smoother and less scratchy than the optical analog switches I have used in the past, especially when pressing a key slowly or typing for longer periods.
They also retain a full 4.0mm range of travel, which is less common than I expected among Hall effect gaming keyboards. I can set a very shallow actuation point for movement keys in competitive games without making the entire board feel like a hair trigger. For typing, I prefer a deeper actuation and the full key travel because it feels more natural and gives me fewer accidental inputs. That flexibility makes the Huntsman V3 HE easier to live with as an everyday keyboard rather than something designed exclusively for ranked matches.
Rapid trigger works as expected, resetting each key based on movement rather than waiting for it to return to a fixed reset point. In shooters, directional inputs feel crisp and immediate, particularly when rapidly stopping, strafing, or changing direction. Snap Tap can prioritize the newest input between two movement keys, while Snap Flex adds another way to activate commands based on releasing a key. These features will matter most to serious FPS players, but the adjustable actuation is useful even outside competitive gaming.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Adam Darling", "review_title": "Elite Magnetic TKL Keyboard With Precision Control", "review_text": "The Razer Huntsman V3 HE Magnetic Tenkeyless is engineered as a competitive‑grade keyboard built around Hall Effect Magnetic Switches, offering adjustable actuation from 0.1 mm to 4.0 mm and a 100‑million keystroke lifespan (). This switch architecture eliminates debounce delay entirely, enabling instantaneous actuation and reset behavior that mechanical switches simply cannot match. The magnetic sensing provides exceptionally consistent input recognition, and the keyboard’s internal calibration system compensates for magnetic interference to maintain stable performance over time. Combined with the TKL layout, which frees up desk space for low‑sensitivity mouse movement, the Huntsman V3 HE is clearly designed for players who rely on precision micro‑adjustments and rapid directional changes.
One of the most defining features is Rapid Trigger, which allows keys to reset the moment they begin to rise rather than waiting for a fixed reset point. This dramatically increases responsiveness in FPS titles, enabling faster counter‑strafes, smoother movement corrections, and more reliable repeated inputs. Esports.gg’s testing highlights how Rapid Trigger transforms WASD control, making movement feel “snappy, predictable, and extremely responsive” — a sentiment that aligns with real‑world gameplay impressions. The keyboard also supports Dynamic Keystroke, allowing up to four actions on a single key at different actuation depths, and Snap Flex, which assigns one action on press and another on release. These features give competitive players granular control over movement, utility activation, and complex keybind setups, especially in games like Valorant, CS2, and Apex Legends ().", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Amazon Customer", "review_title": "Hall Effect Makes The Difference", "review_text": "Huntsman V3 HE Magnetic TKL 8KHz Wired Gaming Keyboard | Hall Effect Magnetic Switches, 8000 Hz Polling, Razer Snap Flex,Razer Snap Tap, Rapid Trigger, Adjustable Actuation
So this listing is for the v3 ten key less Hunstman v3 8K HE keyboard specifically designed for gaming with hall effect switches and snap tap actions. The keyboard has an 8000 Hz polling rate and has onboard memory to store profiles.
I have both the v1 and v2 version of this exact keyboard so comparing all three of these keyboards, they all have the exact same solid build quality and sound quality which is a quite thocky experience. The keyboards are solidly built and made of premium material which leads to a very comfortable typing experience. The keyboard is constructed of a solid plastic and metal material which makes them feel premium. The keyboard is about 14" x 5" x 2" high and weighs in with a heft and weight that allows it to sit solidly on your desk.
I have been using this keyboard exclusively for nearly two weeks now and it is now my daily driver. I am thoroughly impressed by the HE switches and how very comfortable it is to type on. The software is the one short area as the Synapse software really does not effectively work on Mac but it does sort of work on Windows but don't expect much. The keyboard itself is highly customizable and allows for full customization in color along with key press. Also there is no Linux support either but you can use SignalRGB to control lighting. Also Synapse itself really bogs down your PC and slowly causes a memory leak which means you need to regularly reboot your PC.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Terrorgod", "review_title": "Maybe im ready to give Razer another chance", "review_text": "The Razer Huntsman V3 HE Magnetic Mini keyboard is the latest addition to their Hall Effect Magnetic keyboard lineup. If you haven't been keeping up with keyboard technologies, compared to traditional keyboard switches made by companies like Cherry, they are now utilizing magnets and lasers to create a much more responsive key press reducing latency and allowing for customizable key actuation based on the users preference. I am a hobbyist with keyboard tech, where I have built a good variety of keyboards with DIY kits, customized some of my own, and tend to go out of my way to try new technologies. This is my third time trying a Hall Effect keyboard, with my first being the Steelseries Apex Pro ( with HyperMagnetic switches) and the original Razer Huntsman.
I didn't hold onto either of those keyboards very long as at the time they were very expensive compared to their traditional counterparts. They also didn't wow me out of the box with their switch technology. Keypresses felt weak, as if there was no feedback to register that I had hit a key. It also took a lot of tweaking to get them to what I would consider a usable state with accurate typing. Which leaves me with the new Razer Huntsman, where I am happy to report it doesn't share any of these problems.
The recent revisions have made many changes, improving the texture on the keycaps, the sound of the keypresses, the out of box actuation is exactly what I want, and the 8khz polling is probably helping with how responsive the keys feel. I generally use full size keyboards as I like to have a numpad, but the feel of this keyboard is winning me over to make it my daily driver away from my Mountain Everest Max with Cherry Blues. Lubed Holy Panda switches are the only ones I own that might feel a little bit better than these, but the overall responsiveness of these HE Magentics is something I haven't had the pleasure of experiencing before.", "review_rating": ""}]

[{"reviewer_name": "Dani Camacho", "review_title": "Top-notch typing experience! Elegant, quiet, and reliable.", "review_text": "Top-notch typing experience! Elegant, quiet, and reliable.

Tactile feedback and sound level is just right IMO. Battery life is great; I’ve only charged it a few times in nearly a year of daily use. The only downside is the backlighting. [{"reviewer_name": "IKKK", "review_title": "Makes work a joy!", "review_text": "I never thought a keyboard could completely change how I feel about my workday, but this mechanical board is a game-changer. It looks sleek on my desk, types like a dream, and honestly makes me excited to type.

Aesthetic: The white gives off a clean, premium, retro-modern vibe that elevates my desk setup.
Whether you're working on Windows or Mac, if you want a buttery-smooth, incredibly comfortable typing experience that brings a little joy back to the daily grind, this is worth every single penny.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Jay", "review_title": "Luxe and Life Changing ♥️", "review_text": "This is my first ever mechanical keyboard, and I have to say, it's really life changing. [ T H E F E E L ]
The keys with the Specter switches are the creamiest and thockiest! I play a lot of typing games on Steam (both Mac and Win) and this keyboard is the absolute best. I thought I would need time to adapt from my 2007, wired Apple keyboard, but the molded-style PBT keys and overall low profile (with the little kickstand out) are perfect for my accuracy and ergonomics. I don't even have to use a wrist rest. I'm also thankful for the full numpad, which was the deciding factor (alongside the cute, pink color!) between this and other low-pro keyboards. [ C O N N E C T I V I T Y ]
The keyboard connected to my Macbook Air immediately without a problem. Changing between Mac and Win layouts has worked flawlessly. The hitch was that I couldn't use the keyboard software or web portal to change keybinds. Luckily, all the secondary functions on my top row worked with my Mac without a problem.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Isaac Rodriguez", "review_title": "Love it, Software is a bit complicated", "review_text": "This one sounds and feels amazing, the Software is a bit weird, sometimes doesn't recognize correctly the device and had a little bit of trouble to set it up wirelessly, but it ended working great, so far in like a week of use it just loose like a 10% battery charge, so it seems to last quite a while without having to charge it.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Jessica", "review_title": "If you're on the fence, GET IT - you won't regret it!", "review_text": "I could not be happier with this purchase. One thing in particular that I look for is how it feels when I type. The clicks are there both audibly and when you press on the keys (you can feel it), but it is not one of those loud clackers that you see online that will drive your co-workers nuts. It has some weight to it where as it does not feel cheap, but is not overtly heavy. It is compact, so it doesn't take a lot of room up on my desk which I love, and has a very sleek and modern look to it. The only thing I have noticed is that the backspace key feels a bit different and more stiff than the rest of the keys, which are so reactive and that is the one thing that annoys me. You can choose to have the backlit light on or off. I appreciate that it does not have a ton of wacky colors, and instead is a soft white glow that is easy on the eyes and adds a nice look to an already sleek looking keyboard. I feel like the hunt for the perfect office keyboard is officially done!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Van Smith", "review_title": "Good keyboard with horrible wakeup latency", "review_text": "I bought the Lofree Flow Lite 100 Keys Low Profile Mechanical Keyboard after watching several YouTubers enthusiastically endorse it, but I've learned the hard way not to trust keyboard experts who love anime cat themed keyboards most of all and who never review keyboards objectively.
The Flow Lite is not a cheap keyboard regardless of people trying to gaslight you, especially considering its build quality.
It is a nice, compact, thin, illuminated keyboard which includes all keys that are most vital for work but are often dropped or relegated to fn+ status, namely home, end, page up/down, delete and print screen. The key legends are clean and the shine through illumination is even and crisp across nearly every key.
The very light typing experience is pleasant, but there are other keyboards in this price range or even cheaper that are as good or even better. The typing sound is good but nothing spectacular.
The plastic build quality is good but there are many keyboards as good or better in this price range.

Il n'est pas très bruyant comparé à d'autres clavier mécaniques, mais il était encore trop bruyant pour mon usage, alors j'ai remplacé les switchs par les Hades et maintenant il est extrêmement silencieux. The switch between wired/wireless/off is a bit stiff at first but wears in well. I do wish it was more pronounced to be more easy to switch between modes though.
The cable did die super quickly though, for reasons I'm not entirely sure of. I switched the keyboard between wired and wireless, and one time it just didn't want to connect back. Fixed with a replacement cable without problem.
Overall, I like this keyboard. It's as compact as a keyboard with all the necessary keys, can be.", "review_rating": ""}]
